### Transfers: libraries are writable when Studio can reach their files (#705)

## Problem

Transfers took a library location's writable flag from the library registry. There only the main library is writable, because the flag means Studio edits the library through its own file operations and index. So every other library refused copies into it and moves out of it, and read-through libraries were forced read only, even when the files sit in the user's own folder or on a host reached with their own key.

## Rule as built

`LibraryWritable` in `server-go/internal/transfers/access.go` decides from who reaches the files:

| Files reached through | Sign-in off | Sign-in on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main folder | writable | writable |
| Folder on this computer (`SourceRoot`) | writable | read only (server account's permissions are not the viewer's) |
| Library's own host with the viewer's platform key | writable | writable |
| Library's own host over ssh with the server account's keys | writable | not offered (unchanged) |
| Read-through host | writable | not offered (unchanged) |
| Index only | no files | no files |

A read-only library's location `detail` says why, and the plan's refusal repeats it.

## Pre-flight write check

Before a plan is offered, it makes and removes a `.studio-transfer-probe-<id>` folder in the destination folder, and for a move in the folders the originals leave (the folder holding each item named and each folder named, at most 8). This is the Settings connection test's pattern (`Mkdir` then `RemoveStaging`), so it works on `LocalFS`, `RemoteFS` with a shell, and `RemoteFS` over SFTP. A failure is a 400: `you cannot write in <folder> on <host> (<label>), so ...`. It runs for every location kind, and again when a plan is confirmed. Deeper folders in a move are not probed. A removal failure there already leaves the originals and the landed copy in place and fails the transfer with the count not removed (`land.go`), which is unchanged.

## Index staleness

Only the main library is re-indexed after a transfer. Plans and transfers gain `indexNotes`: for a library other than the main one that the transfer writes into or moves out of, "The index of <label> shows this change after its next rebuild in Settings, Indexing, Libraries" (a library Studio builds, here or remote) or "after the index is rebuilt where it is built" (an index connected as it is, including read-through). The finished transfer's events repeat it. Refreshing the affected folders of a non-main library that Studio builds is left for later: the only existing incremental path (`kb.ReindexRoots`) is bound to the main library's indexer.

## Web and chat

The web already drives the "Read only" badge and disabled controls from `writable`, so libraries writable by access now show as writable. The plan dialog, the chat plan card and the transfer drawer show `indexNotes` as info callouts. The chat tools call the same `Plan`, so the rule and the pre-flight check apply to them; the started result and the end note in the conversation carry the index notes.

## Tests

- `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` in server-go pass.
- New `access_test.go`: the rule table; copy into and move out of a non-main LocalFS library with sign-in off, and refusals with sign-in on; a RemoteFS library through the viewer's key with sign-in on; a read-through library with sign-in off; the pre-flight refusal for a 0555 folder on this computer, on a shell host (stand-in runner) and over SFTP; staleness notes in the plan, the transfer and its events. The test rig's second library now follows the rule, and the old "read only" refusal cases moved to the sign-in-on test.
- Chat: the end note carries the index notes.
- Web: `tsc` passes; vitest for chatTransferPlan, transfersPage, transfers and transfersHelp pass, with a new case for the index note on the chat card.

Docs: docs/TRANSFERS.md and docs/HELP.md.

### Transfers: use older rsync where it is safe, chosen by capability (#707)

## Problem

The rsync mover decided by version number: 3.0.0 on every end (for `-s` and `--no-inc-recursive`), and 3.2.5 on this computer for a pull. macOS ships rsync 2.6.9 or openrsync, so a Mac never used rsync, not even for a copy between two of its own folders. RHEL 8 and 9 ship 3.1.3 and 3.2.3 with security fixes backported under the old number, so a number check refused them. The two ends of a transfer often run different releases, and rsync negotiates its protocol but not its options, so an option the far end does not know makes it fail.

## What changes

Each end's rsync is read once and kept five minutes: `--version`, `--help` (GNU's option list or openrsync's usage synopsis; only the option column is read), and a `--trust-sender --version` probe. A host's is read through the remote helper as before. Each option is then given only when the end or ends that must understand it have it. Which end needs what follows `server_options()` in rsync's `options.c` (checked in 3.0.9 and 3.4.1), cited in a comment on `rsyncDecide`:

| Option | Needed on | Given when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-s` | both ends | both have `--protect-args` or `--secluded-args`; pull, push and host to host only |
| `--timeout=120` | both ends (always passed on) | both have it |
| `--max-size` | the receiver (passed on when the client sends) | the receiver has it |
| `--no-inc-recursive` | the client only (it clears the `i` in `-e.`) | the client is GNU rsync with protocol 30 or later |
| `--info=progress2` | the client only | the client has `--info` |
| `--chmod`, `--files-from`, `--from0` (or `-0`) | the client | required; missing means no rsync, and the reason names the option |
| `--files-from=-`, `--from0` | the sending host, in a pull | required there |

`--chmod` is never passed on: the sender applies it in `send_file_name` and the receiver in `recv_file_entry`, so the client's own is enough.

Without protect args the far folder passes through the far end's shell. It is quoted in single quotes (with `'\''`) when the client passes it on as is (2.6.9 to 3.2.3, openrsync), and gets only wildcard escapes when the client escapes the rest itself (3.2.4 and later, detected by `--old-args`; `safe_arg` leaves `*?[]` for the remote shell). File names only ever travel in the `--files-from` list. `RSYNC_OLD_ARGS` and `RSYNC_PROTECT_ARGS` are removed from rsync's environment here and through `env -u` on a host.

Routes:
- Here (both ends on this computer): any rsync with the required options.
- Push: the same here, any release on the host. `-s` when both ends have it, else the quoted folder.
- Pull: this computer's rsync must be 3.2.5 or later, or accept `--trust-sender`. Otherwise the reason names CVE-2022-29154 and Studio copy carries it. The host needs `--files-from` and `--from0`.
- On one host: the host's rsync with the required options; no shell between ends.
- Host to host: the source host's rsync with the required options; any release on the destination.

On macOS with the default setting (`rsync`), `/opt/homebrew/bin/rsync` and `/usr/local/bin/rsync` are tried along with PATH's, and the most capable is used (can pull, then protect args, then newer). The desktop app does take the login shell's PATH (`deploy/mac/studio-run.sh`), so Homebrew's rsync was found when that PATH puts Homebrew ahead of `/usr/bin`, but not otherwise, since the fallback PATH and `FindRsync`'s own list put `/usr/bin` first. An explicit path in Settings is always used as is.

Settings and the Ready line now say what the rsync found is used for, for example `rsync 2.6.9 at /usr/bin/rsync: used on this computer and for sends to hosts; pulls use Studio copy (needs rsync 3.2.5 or a build with the CVE-2022-29154 fix)`. The connection test says the same of a host's rsync. New fields: `detected.rsyncPath`, `detected.rsyncText`, and `rsyncText` on the test result. Plan reasons say when the folder is quoted because an end has no `--protect-args`.

Studio uses the rsync installed on each end.

## Findings

- macOS openrsync (man page in Xcode): has `--files-from`, `-0`/`--from0`, `--chmod`, `--max-size`, `--timeout`, `-t`, `--rsync-path`, `-e`; no `-s`, `--info`, `--no-inc-recursive` or `--trust-sender`; protocol 27 to 29. OpenBSD's openrsync has no `--files-from` and is not used.
- RHEL 8 (CentOS Stream 8 `rsync.spec`): the CVE-2022-29154 fix landed in 3.1.3-18 (August 2022); `rsync-3.1.3-trust-sender.patch` came with 3.1.3-23 (May 2025, RHEL-52004). That patch adds the option but no `--help` line, hence the probe. A build from -18 to -22 is fixed but is refused for pulls, since nothing marks it.
- RHEL 9: CentOS Stream 9 is now on 3.2.5 and later (3.2.7), which passes on version. I did not confirm whether the earlier 3.2.3 RHEL 9 builds accept `--trust-sender`; those are refused for pulls unless they do.

## Tests

- `TestRsyncCapsFromHelp`: fake `--version`/`--help` for GNU 2.6.9, 3.0.9, 3.1.3, 3.1.3 with `--trust-sender`, 3.2.3, 3.2.7, 3.4.1, macOS openrsync and OpenBSD openrsync.
- `TestRsyncArgvAcrossVersions`: exact argv or refusal for every route, crossing this computer's and the host's versions (2.6.9 with 3.1.3, openrsync with 3.2.7, 3.4.1 with 2.6.9, 3.1.3 with `--trust-sender` with 3.0.9, both 3.4.1, and more), with a destination root holding spaces, a quote, `$()` and wildcards.
- `TestRemotePathThroughShell`: the quoted and escaped forms come through `sh` unchanged.
- `TestRsyncFindsHomebrew`: Homebrew before PATH on a stand-in Mac, the best one picked, an explicit path respected, and the Settings text.
- `TestSystemRsync`: the system `/usr/bin/rsync` run with the argv Studio builds: a copy here, a push and a pull through a stand-in remote shell, with and without `-s`, and the single-quoted form. Added to the macOS job, so it runs against the rsync macOS ships.
- Existing tests pass, including `TestOverRealSSH` with `STUDIO_TEST_SSHD=1` locally (rsync 3.2.7). `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and the web suite pass.

## Left for later

- Progress for clients without `--info` (2.6.9, openrsync) is reported when each group ends.
- A pull from an openrsync host is allowed by its listed options; no openrsync server was available to try it.

### Transfers: rclone remotes as locations, and rclone as a mover (#708)

Transfers gains rclone: each remote of the installed rclone's configuration is a location, and rclone is a mover for transfers with a remote at one end and this computer or another remote at the other.

**Product rules**
- Studio uses the installed rclone and never bundles it. It looks in this order: the path set in Settings, Transfers (default `rclone`); on macOS, `/opt/homebrew/bin/rclone` and `/usr/local/bin/rclone`; then `PATH`.
- Studio never writes rclone's configuration. Remotes come from `rclone listremotes --long` (names and types, no secrets) and are named in rclone's own commands, so `RCLONE_CONFIG` and the rest apply as the user set them. When rclone is missing or has no remotes, Settings and the Ready line say so, and nothing else changes.
- Single-user only. With sign-in on there are no `rclone` locations, the mover refuses a signed-in viewer's plan, and the managed settings switch rclone off, following saved locations and CONDUIT.

**Locations**
- New kind `rclone`, id `rclone:<remote>`, one per configured remote, rooted at the remote's top. Browsable in the two-pane view, usable from the assistant's transfer tools (the catalog's mover enum and descriptions name it), with a cloud icon and the group "rclone remotes" in the picker.
- `RcloneFS` (`fs_rclone.go`) maps the FS interface to rclone subcommands, each name its own argv element after `--`, never a shell:

| FS call | rclone |
| --- | --- |
| List, Walk | `lsjson`, `lsjson -R` streamed and stopped at the file limit, always `--no-mimetype --use-server-modtime` |
| Stat | `lsjson --stat` for up to 16 paths on a file system; otherwise a listing of the folders holding them |
| Read, Write | `cat`; `rcat --metadata --metadata-set mtime=...` after checking the name is free |
| Mkdir, Free | `mkdir`; `about --json` where the backend has About |
| Sha256 | `lsjson --hash --hash-type sha256` where the backend has it, else read through `cat` and hashed here |
| Land | one `move --files-from-raw` of exactly the staged files, after checking each final name |
| Remove | one `delete --files-from-raw` with `--max-delete` equal to the number of files, then `rmdir` deepest first (skipped on object stores) |
| RemoveStaging | `purge`, only for a staging-named folder; not found counts as removed |

- Containment: paths are checked by `CleanRel` like every location's, and rclone's local backend skips links. Features come from `rclone backend features` (its output has trailing commas, which are stripped), cached ten minutes.
- Object stores have no folders. `Mkdir` makes nothing below a bucket, a path with no objects lists as empty and can be a destination (a sync into a new prefix plans as empty), folders vanish with their last object, so `Remove` does no `rmdir` there. S3 answers `lsjson --stat` for a missing path with a folder and status 0, so on object stores Stat lists the parent folder, and falls back to `--stat` when the parent cannot be listed (anonymous access to a public bucket cannot list the buckets).

**Mover**
- Order is conduit, rsync, rclone, studio-copy. rsync now refuses rclone ends. rclone is offered when one end is an rclone remote and the other is this computer or another remote. The plan's reason names the ends and the staging mode, or says why not (sign-in on, neither end a remote, a cluster or ssh host at the other end).
- Always `rclone copy`, also for move and sync, with the plan's file list:

```
rclone copy --files-from-raw <list> --no-traverse --use-json-log --stats 1s --stats-log-level NOTICE \
  --transfers <n> --checkers <n> [--ignore-existing | --ignore-times] -- <src> <dst>
```

  The reason: Studio's plan decides what goes and Studio checks what arrived before it deletes anything. `rclone move` would delete originals before that check, and `rclone sync` would delete what its own listing found extra, which is not necessarily what the plan showed.
- Progress comes from the JSON stats line (`stats.bytes`, `stats.transfers`). I chose this over `--progress` because it is one JSON object per line and needs no terminal-output parsing. Error text is taken from the last `error` level JSON line.
- Cancel sends an interrupt, so rclone aborts multipart uploads, and kills after 15 s (`cmd.Cancel` and `WaitDelay`).
- Transfers between an rclone remote and a cluster or ssh host use studio-copy, with `cat`/`rcat` on the rclone side. Studio never configures a remote to reach a host.

**Staging decision**
- On a remote with server-side rename (`Move` feature: file systems, SFTP, most drives), rclone writes into the staging folder and files take their names after the check, the same guarantee as every other mover.
- On a remote without it (object stores), landing a staged object is a server-side copy of every byte plus a delete. That doubles the work for large data. So the rclone mover writes straight to the final names (`plan.direct`). The trade-off:
  - Guaranteed: an object store shows an object only once its upload is complete, so nothing appears half written. Files the plan does not list as replaced are sent with `--ignore-existing`, so a name that appeared since the plan is not overwritten. Listed replacements are sent with `--ignore-times`. Studio checks each file's size (and hash for a move or with checksum) at its final name before it removes originals or deletes extras.
  - Not guaranteed: if the transfer fails or is cancelled, objects already sent stay, and a replaced object is replaced when its new copy arrives, before the check.
  - The plan states this as a warning, and the reason text says which mode applies.
  - studio-copy into an object store (from a cluster or ssh host) still stages, so that path keeps the full guarantee at the cost of the server-side copy.

**Sync comparison and checks**
- With an rclone end, a sync compares size plus a hash both ends have, preferring MD5 (an object store gives it from its listing; this computer reads its files). It falls back to size and modification time for a file with no such hash, such as an S3 multipart object, or when the ends share no hash. The plan has a new `compare` field showing which rule applied, and the confirm dialog shows it under "Compared by".
- Verification for a move or with checksum uses the shared hash in place of sha256 when one end is a remote, so an S3 object is not downloaded again. A file without the shared hash falls back to sha256.

**Settings and Ready line**
- Settings, Transfers, How files move has an rclone block: on/off switch, Program path, "Found at <path>, version <v>" or the plain reason it is missing, and a table of remotes with their types (or "rclone has no remotes. Add them with `rclone config`").
- `detected.rclone` is `{ enabled, found, path, version, remotes, why }`. `movers.rclone` is `{ enabled, path }`. The path is a bare name or an absolute path, and spaces are allowed in absolute paths because rclone is run directly. rclone is also a choice for the default mover.
- The Ready line counts "N rclone remotes", or says "rclone not found" or "rclone has no remotes" when rclone is on.
- Host detection: the helper has an `rclone` command (`command -v rclone`, then its version). A saved location's test reports `rclone`/`rcloneVersion`, shown as information. Clusters have no location test in the UI yet.

**Coordination**
- Rebased on #705 (library writable). Its write probe works on rclone locations: on object stores `Mkdir` is a no-op and the probe always passes.
- Edits to shared files are small and additive: `plan.go` (direct flag, sync rule hook, a 404 allowance for object-store sync destinations, mover list text), `land.go` (verify through `verifySums`/`verifyDirect`, no landing in direct mode), `jobs.go` (direct mode skips the staging folder), `rsync.go` (refuses rclone ends), `settings*.go`, the helper's one `rclone` line in `fs_remote.go`, and two tests that count movers (3 to 4).

**Tests**
- Fake rclone: the test binary re-executed through a script on `PATH` (`rclone_fake_test.go`). It keeps remotes in folders, one behaving as S3 (no rename, no empty folders, MD5 only, `.parts` objects without MD5, `--stat` answering a missing path as a folder). It prints rclone's listremotes, version, features (with trailing commas), lsjson and JSON stats, and logs every argv.
- `rclone_test.go` covers:
  - discovery order, including Homebrew on darwin and a set path with spaces;
  - detection: found, missing, no remotes, off, sign-in on;
  - settings validation;
  - locations and the sign-in refusal (no locations, 404 on browse, mover refusal);
  - every FS method on both kinds, including a name with spaces and quotes, `--` before each spec, the fast listing flags on every lsjson, the walk limit, land conflicts and replace, `--max-delete`, and `RemoveStaging` refusing a non-staging folder;
  - mover argv for staging, new and replace;
  - stats and message parsing;
  - copy, move and sync through jobs, including the direct mode, MD5 verification, `--ignore-times` for replacements, sync and copy into an empty prefix, and refusal of a name already in the store;
  - the time fallback for an object with no MD5;
  - cancel mid-copy (nothing left in place, no staging);
  - remote to ssh host and back via studio-copy;
  - host detection.
- `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `scripts/crossvet.sh` pass. Web: `tsc` and vitest (both configs) pass; new tests cover the settings block, the Ready line and the plain rules.
- End to end with real rclone v1.76.0, a scratch server on 127.0.0.1 with sign-in off and its own data folders, and a scratch `RCLONE_CONFIG` with two alias remotes (the user's own rclone config was not read or touched). Over HTTP:
  - browse;
  - copy this computer to remote;
  - sync with one change and one extra deleted (compare: size and md5);
  - sync remote to remote, then a second plan with 0 files;
  - move remote to this computer (md5 verified);
  - move remote to remote;
  - no staging folders left anywhere.
- Also end to end:
  - a cancel of a 6 GB copy stopped rclone and removed the staging folder;
  - an anonymous read from a public S3 bucket (2 small objects) listed with the fast flags and was verified by MD5 from the listing;
  - the settings PUT took an absolute path and refused a relative one.

**Limits and later**
- Direct writes to a writable object store were tested against the fake only; no writable S3 endpoint was available here.
- On S3, the write probe from #705 cannot detect a read-only bucket before the transfer. The transfer then fails on the first write.
- With no shared hash, a sync to an object store resends same-size files, because listed times are upload times.
- Later: rclone remotes as Studio libraries; a location rooted at a folder inside a remote (`RcloneFS.Base` exists, but there is no setting for it yet); rclone run on clusters or ssh hosts; a location test for clusters.

## v1.200.3 (2026-11-15)

### Test flakes: stream signals in TestStreamsAreNotBuffered, the Transfers page in transfersNav (#702)

TestStreamsAreNotBuffered failed now and then in CI with "event 1 is \"\"". Its fake Node shared one unbuffered signal channel across every request it got, and any request the server's background jobs make to Node landed in the same streaming handler and waited on that channel, so it could take a signal meant for a stream. Each stream now has its own channel, keyed by its path, and the fake Node answers any other request with a 404 at once. The handler waits up to 30 s for its signal, the test gives up on a send after 10 s with a clear message, and a stream that ends early says so in place of an empty event.

transfersNav.test.tsx failed on both runners in this PR's first CI run. Its two "left out" tests waited for the address to change and then checked at once that the Transfers page was gone, but the app changes the address before the render that removes the page. They now wait for the page to go.

Ran the Go test 30 times with the race detector and the whole server package, and the web test five times, locally.

### Transfers: SFTP-only ssh locations over SFTP (#703)

## What changed

Transfers can now use a saved ssh location, or a host location, whose account takes SFTP only (OpenSSH `ForceCommand internal-sftp`, usually with a chroot). Such an account answers every command with `This service allows sftp connections only.` and status 1, so the bash helper in `fs_remote.go` could not browse or copy.

- **Detection.** On first use of a plain ssh site, Studio runs `true` there once. The SFTP-only answer (OpenSSH prints it on standard output) marks the site as SFTP only for 10 minutes; a shell answer marks it as a shell host for the same time. A helper call that later gets the SFTP-only answer marks the site and asks for a retry. Sites reached through pw ssh, and runners without a subsystem, are never probed.
- **SFTP client.** `remote.Pool.Subsystem` builds `ssh -s <destination> sftp` from `sshBase`, so the site's options, port, BatchMode and ControlMaster sharing all apply. Transfers reaches it through an optional `Subsystemer` interface on the Runner (`PoolRunner` has it), so existing fake Runners compile unchanged. The client is `github.com/pkg/sftp` (BSD-2).
- **FS.** `RemoteFS` stays the one type. Each method takes the SFTP path (`fs_sftp.go`) for an SFTP-only site, opening a session per call and closing it after; `Read`'s closer ends the session. The helper's rules hold: hidden entries left out of listings and walks, links never followed, a missing path a 404 and a link a 400 in a walk, every real folder inside the real root, exclusive writes with folders made and mtime and u+x set, landing never over a name the plan did not list (hard link, else SFTP rename; `posix-rename` for a listed replacement), removal of plain files then empty folders deepest first, and recursive removal only of a staging folder, never through a link. Free space comes from `statvfs@openssh.com`. Sha256 reads each file over the session and hashes it in Studio.
- **Movers.** rsync refuses an SFTP-only location with that reason, so studio-copy carries the transfer; its plan line says "over SFTP".
- **Settings.** The connection test returns `sftpOnly: true`, skips the rsync probe, and the web page says the account takes SFTP only, that copies use Studio copy over SFTP, and that rsync is not available there.
- **Docs.** HELP.md, README.md, docs/README.md and docs/TRANSFERS.md.

One change from the first design: path containment does not rely on the server's realpath. Some SFTP servers (pkg/sftp's own) only clean the path and do not resolve links, so Studio finds each real folder by looking up each name with lstat and readlink, from the root's real path, cached for the call.

## How it was tested

- `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` in server-go pass.
- New unit tests run pkg/sftp's server over in-process pipes, with no ssh: every FS method, root containment through links (including a linked root), links in listings and walks, exclusive create, land with and without replace, remove, staging removal, free space, session cleanup, detection and caching, and plans and transfers through the service (studio-copy chosen, rsync refused, a push, a move back with checksum, the settings test).
- `remote.Pool.Subsystem` argv test.
- `STUDIO_TEST_SSHD=1` run: the real-sshd harness gains a third host with `ForceCommand internal-sftp`; browse, push, move back with checksum and the settings test pass over real ssh.
- Web: vitest for the Settings test result text.
- End to end against a real chrooted SFTP-only account on a test host, through a scratch Studio server's HTTP API with a throwaway key: settings test (`sftpOnly: true`, writable, free space), browse, a copy of a folder of four files to the upload folder and back (hashes and mtimes match), a move of one file in, a refused copy over an existing name, a copy with replace, a move of the folder back out with checksum (originals and folders removed from the host), and rsync named explicitly refused. No staging folders were left. The key and test files were removed afterwards.

### Transfers: copy, move and sync between libraries, this computer, clusters, ssh hosts and CONDUIT (#700)

A Transfers page for copying, moving and syncing files between libraries, folders on this computer, ACTIVATE clusters, other computers over ssh and CONDUIT. There are matching tools for the assistant. This goes to a Preview build for testing before any Stable release.

## The page

- The activity list is the default view. Active transfers come first, with progress, rate and time left. Finished ones are paged 50 at a time from the server, with search and filters, and stay quick with thousands kept (180 days, at most 10,000).
- **New transfer** opens two panes with location pickers and drill-down file lists. A Start button points each way.
- Copy, move and sync (new and changed files, with deletions only when ticked). Every transfer shows its plan before it starts: what goes where, the file count and size, what is replaced or deleted, and the mover.
- The sidebar entry shows how many transfers are under way, and a warning after a failure. The pages setting has a Transfers switch.

## Server (`server-go/internal/transfers`)

- **Locations:** libraries, folders on this computer (Downloads, Desktop, Documents and added ones), the viewer's clusters over `pw ssh`, saved ssh locations, the hosts libraries are on, and CONDUIT paths.
- **Movers:** rsync (pull, push, on-host and host to host), Studio's own copy through the server, and CONDUIT through an attached MCP server. CONDUIT is sent COPY only, and Studio verifies the result and removes originals itself.
- **Staging:** every job writes into `.studio-transfer-<id>`. Files take their names only after the count and sizes (or sha256) check. A mover that reports success on a bad result fails the job.
- **Limits:** at most three jobs at once. A transfer into the main library is indexed when it ends.
- **Sign-in on:** each person sees only their own transfers and uses their own platform key. Settings come from `STUDIO_TRANSFER_*` environment variables, and the settings routes answer 403.
- **Shared code:** `mcpclient` keeps `structuredContent` and `isError`, and `remote` gains streaming commands.

## Settings, Transfers

- A summary of what is ready with no setup.
- Saved locations, each tested before it is saved, with port and ssh options under Advanced.
- Folders on this computer, library hosts, how files move (rsync path, streams, CONDUIT and its folder mapping), and defaults.
- The setup wizard's last step says how many places are ready.

## Assistant

- Tools: `transfer_locations`, `browse_location`, `transfer_files`, `transfer_status`, `cancel_transfer`.
- A plan that cannot run goes back to the model with its reason. A valid one is held for approval with the plan on the card, and the Transfers list shows it as awaiting approval.
- **Yes** starts the transfer, and the tool returns at once. **No**, or a hold that expires, cancels it.
- When the transfer ends, a note is added to the conversation. The chat page shows the note without a reload, and a question sent before it arrives is placed after it. A link `#view=transfers?transfer=<id>` opens the transfer.

## Docs

- HELP.md has a Transfers section.
- docs/TRANSFERS.md covers the server and the HTTP contract.
- The documents index and README are updated.

## Tested

- `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass. Tests run over two real sshd processes, and against a fake MCP server for CONDUIT.
- Web: 76 files, 580 tests pass, and the build passes.
- Against a real server through the UI: a copy of 1,503 files (1.3 GB, byte-identical on spot checks), a move, and a sync (a second identical sync sent nothing). Progress was followed on a 5.9 GB copy.
- 2,000 finished transfers page in the browser: 380 to 560 ms for the first page and 60 to 125 ms for each further page.
- Against a real ACTIVATE cluster through the API (pw ssh):
  - A copy from this computer with rsync: 4 files, sha256 identical, and no staging folder left.
  - A sync back with Studio's copy: identical.
  - A move off the cluster with rsync: identical, with the originals removed.
- Against a real model: an assistant copy (approved, returned at once, note written once) and a sync with deletions (denied, record cancelled, nothing deleted). A transfer outlived the reply and the client closing.

## Not yet tested

- Saved hosts and library hosts over real ssh from the page.
- CONDUIT against a running service.
- Sign-in on against a real server.

### Reports: written once, edited in place; agent status looked at again (#692)

Writing a report from the chat sent the whole document once per format, and again in full for every correction. This change has the report written once and edited in place.

**Reports**
- `write_kb_file` takes `also` (pdf, docx, or both) with a Markdown path: the documents are made beside it under its name in the same call.
- `write_kb_file` takes `source` in place of `content`: a PDF, Word or Excel file made from a text file already in the library.

- The record of which document was made from which file is kept beside the index (`made-documents.json`).

**Chat loop**
- A repeated tool call in one reply is no longer answered from the reply's cache when the tool reads live state (agent, run, session, cluster and task status), and a call that changes something clears the cache. An agent's status asked for twice now returns its state at each ask.

- The follow-up suggestions route compared the conversation's owner name with the viewer's id, so it answered 403 for every signed-in owner with per-person history. It compares usernames.

### Report rendering: whole words in tables, footnotes, checklists, page header and footer (#693)

Reports written from the chat as PDF and Word documents had tables with split words, characters that vanished, and no way to mark every page. This change fixes the layout and adds the options a report needs.

**Tables**
- A column is never narrower than its longest word while the table can fit, and the table is as wide as the text column, in the PDF and in Word.
- PDF cells keep bold, italic, code and links. Word column widths come from font metrics.
- A table too wide for the page steps its text and padding down, then breaks only the longest words, and is reported so the assistant can turn the page to landscape or split the table.
- Word rows do not split across pages; a header row stays with its first row in both formats.

**Text**
- A character the PDF font lacks is given an equivalent or a placeholder and reported. It was dropped silently.
- Footnotes are numbered and listed under a Notes heading. A footnote nothing refers to is reported; the parser leaves it out.
- Task list items draw a checked or empty box.
- Word: a justified line that ends at a line break is no longer stretched; the document opens out of compatibility mode.

**Options**
- Front matter takes `header`, `footer` and `spacing`.

**Layout**
- A heading stays with what follows it, a figure with its caption, a caption with its table. A tall picture is drawn smaller when most of the page is free.

**Chat**
- The result of a write or an edit names what went wrong in making a document in one sentence.
- Asking for a code session by that name brings the agent tools into the reply.

**Tests**
- `quality_test.go`, `agentcue_test.go`.

**Docs**
- HELP.md, README.md and GO-PORT.md.

margin (0.5 to 2 inches). Unknown keys and values out of range are
listed in the result so the model can correct them. A line holding only
\newpage (or \pagebreak, \clearpage, or <!-- pagebreak -->) starts a new
page.

The PDF lays out justified paragraphs word by word, as fpdf justifies
only single-style cells, keeping bold, italic and links; a serif font
uses the first complete Liberation Serif, Times New Roman or DejaVu
Serif family found. Word documents get the font and size in their
default style, justified body and list paragraphs, the page size,
orientation and margins in the section, and a page number footer. Word
tables now stay inside the margins after their indent.

HTML pages in the viewer may open the print dialog (allow-modals in the
frame and the CSP sandbox), and a Print button opens the page in a tab
of its own that prints it, with Save as PDF among the destinations.

### pw code from the chat: library folders, finding sessions, waiting (#689)

start_agent works in a library folder when the site sees this Studio's
library: always the local site, and a cluster where a mark file written
here reads back over pw ssh (the same machine, or the library on shared
storage). The folder is the one named with the new folder argument, or a
new one under agents/; elsewhere it keeps ~/studio-agents. A named
folder on a site that does not see the library is refused.

agent_status takes wait (up to 600 seconds), holding while the agent
works, through a goal's turns, until it finishes or asks for approval.
It reports the session's last error, and once the agent is not running
it indexes its library folder and lists the files there with links.

agent_sessions takes find, matching a session's name, the topic pw code
gave it, its first request and its workspace, and lists each session's
topic and first request. The other agent tools accept a session's name
or topic words in place of its id; when several match as well, the
result lists them so the model asks which.

The agent tools are offered without the platform where the Studio offers
its own host as a site (sign-in off, or AGENT_LOCAL_SITE=1), as pw code
runs without an ACTIVATE account.

Checked end to end against a pw code daemon on a development host: start_agent made the session in a new library folder, agent_status found it by topic words, waited for it to finish, indexed the folder and linked the file it wrote; a session that stopped on a model error now says so.

## v1.198 (2026-11-13)

### Reports: image paths may hold spaces; a PDF rewritten in place shows its new pages (#686)

Two problems that kept a screenshot out of a chat-written PDF report, found in use on v1.197.

**Spaces in image paths.** A macOS screenshot's name has spaces (`Screenshot 2026-11-13 at 9.01.28 AM.png`). Markdown ends a bare link destination at the first space, so `![alt](uploads/chat/Screenshot ... .png)` was not parsed as an image, and the model had to copy and rename the file. `docwrite.Parse` now wraps such a destination in angle brackets first. One level of parentheses is allowed (`(2).png`). A destination with a title and text inside code fences are left as written. The tool description says spaces are fine.

**Old pages after a rewrite.** Three causes:

- **Server:** `PagePNG` re-rendered a page whose PDF was newer than its cached image. But pdftoppm writes `p-N.png`, and the rename to `pN.png` ran only when `pN.png` was missing, so the old image was served forever. The pattern that found the new file also matched `pN.png` itself. The stale image is now removed before rendering, and the cached name is skipped when looking for the new one.
- **Browser cache:** page images (`/api/kb/pdf-page`) and pictures inside Office files (`/api/kb/office-media`) were cached for five minutes (`max-age=300`). They now send `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` with an ETag from the source file's mtime and size and the page or name. A matching `If-None-Match` gets 304 before anything is rendered.
- **Viewer:** a page reuses an image it already holds for a URL, whatever the headers say. Page-image, pdf.js and image URLs now carry `v=<mtime>`, and the paged preview is keyed by path and mtime.

Tests:
- `kb/pagepng_rewrite_test.go` renders page 1, rewrites the PDF and renders again. It fails on main and passes here, and is skipped without poppler.
- `kb/fresh_test.go` covers 304, per-page tags and a rewritten file.
- `docwrite/images_test.go` covers spaced, parenthesized, titled, fenced and bracketed paths.
- `chat/docimages_test.go` writes a PDF that embeds a spaced screenshot name.
- The web test is updated for the versioned URL.

Checked live on a local Studio: a three-page PDF open in the viewer was rewritten in place as a one-page PDF, opened again, and showed the new page.

## v1.197 (2026-11-13)

### GUFI 0.8.1 (#679)

Moves the Studio from GUFI 0.8.0 to 0.8.1 (tag 0.8.1, commit f2292ea5), a fix release with the same index format.

Upstream changes that touch the Studio:

- Library links and rpaths are fixed: the install now makes `libvec0` and `liblembed0` relative links in the build directory. The lean Linux build's `deploy/common/gufi-no-lembed.patch` no longer applied (its install hunks failed) and is ported to the new install section. The existing step that replaces absolute links in the tree still runs and now finds none to replace.
- `gufi_vt(internal_copy=...)` is split into `internal_test` and `internal_copy`. The Studio does not use either.
- GUFI now sets `PRAGMA trusted_schema = ON`. No Studio query depends on it.
- `spread_tree.c` now creates its file with `mkstemp`, so the `setup_gufi.sh` fix for the missing `open` mode no longer matches. It is conditional and is left in place for older refs.

Pins updated: `indexer/setup_gufi.sh`, `deploy/common/pins.sh` (Linux and macOS builds), `deploy/app.def`, `deploy/gufi-index.yaml`, the macOS package fallback in `deploy/mac/build_app.sh` (0.8.1 pkg and its SHA-256; the GUFI license is unchanged), `GUFI_RELEASE` in `mac-app.yml` (new prerelease `gufi-f2292ea-macos14`, built by `gufi-macos.yml` from the tag), the upgrade e2e version check, the wfparser golden file (regenerated), and the docs.

Tested:

- The lean Linux build (`deploy/linux/build_gufi.sh`, `GUFI_LEMBED=0`) in `rockylinux:8`, as `linux-app.yml` runs it: builds in 3 minutes, and its own `gufi_dir2index` and `gufi_query` check passes. Manifest: GUFI 0.8.1, SQLite 3.53.4, sqlite-vec 0.1.10-alpha.4, PCRE2 10.49, glibc 2.28.
- The Go suite with `GUFI_BIN` and `STUDIO_GUFI_BIN` pointed at that tree, compared with the same run against the 0.8.0 lean tree: 678 pass, 47 skip, 3 fail, against 677, 48, 3 on 0.8.0. The one difference is `TestRemoteTreeOfARolledUpIndex`, which was skipped on 0.8.0 (no `gufi_rollup` in that tree) and passes on 0.8.1. The same three tests fail on both versions because of where this host installs GUFI (the SSH library tests expect `/opt/gufi/bin`).
- 0.8.1 tools read an index that 0.8.0 wrote and give the same rows, including `dev`.

macOS:

- `gufi-f2292ea-macos14` is published as a prerelease that is never marked latest, so v1.196 stays the latest release. It is the full build (SQLite 3.53.4, sqlite-vec 0.1.10-alpha.4, sqlite-lembed 0.0.1-alpha.8, llama.cpp, libomp 23.1.4, PCRE2 10.49), like `gufi-021a717-macos14`. `check_gufi.sh` passed on the build runner and on a clean `macos-15` runner: index, query, embed and search.
- Two fixes to `gufi-macos.yml` were needed to publish it. First, GitHub no longer runs `macos-14` runners, so the check job was cancelled at start and the release job never ran. The default check runner is now `macos-15`. The build still targets macOS 14, but no hosted runner checks that version any more. Second, a `gufi-*` tag push built the lean GUFI, although the workflow comment says a tag push gives the full build. On a push `inputs.lembed` is null, and `null == false` is true in a workflow expression, so the expression now checks the event first.

Upgrade e2e (`mac-upgrade-e2e`, which runs here because its script changed):

- The test installs v1.183 and builds libraries at each depth, then replaces it with this build. With this PR it passes. The update touched none of the 141 index databases. All 57 answers matched before and after the update, and again after every library was rebuilt with 0.8.1.
- It first failed on 7 answers. A control run on main, updating v1.183 to the released v1.196 (GUFI 0.8.0), failed on the same 7. The rows were identical once sorted, and only the column labels differed. The Node server in v1.183 labels an unnamed result column `col1`, and the Go server labels it with its expression (`count(*)`). The comparison now treats a `colN` label as matching the label in the same position. This check had last run on 2 November, before the Go server shipped.
- A rerun of the `mac-app` build was needed once, after `hdiutil convert` returned "Resource temporarily unavailable".

### Chat: move, rename, copy and delete library files; a delete waits for approval (#680)

The chat can now move, rename, copy and delete files in the main library.

- `move_kb_files` (paths, dest, optional name) and `copy_kb_files` (paths, dest) use the Library's own move and copy (`kb.Files`), create the destination folder when missing, and re-index the roots touched. A move never replaces a file: a taken name is skipped and reported. A copy into a folder that has the name is named "<name> copy". They run at once.
- `rename_kb_file` (path, name) renames one file or folder where it is. It is the rename `move_kb_files` does with a name and no dest, under a name the model finds when asked to rename something.
- `delete_kb_files` (paths) is held for the user's approval through the existing approval path (held-tool-calls.json, the approval card, resume). The card is headed "Delete N files?", lists the paths one per line, and says the Studio cannot undo it. Preparing the call refuses missing paths, folders and protected folders before anything is asked. After Yes, `kb.Files.DeletePaths` deletes the files with their caches and re-indexes.
- Library changes have their own gate (`kbChangesAvailable`): someone present to approve and a conversation that is theirs. They need no platform key, unlike cluster and run changes. The MCP endpoint and no-viewer callers still never get a tool that asks first.
- The tools are in the editing group, whose cue now includes delete, remove, clean up, move, rename, copy and archive, and in Settings, Tools.

Moves between libraries or systems are left to the data movers.

Tests: `kbfileops_test.go` (path parsing; move, rename, refused overwrite, copy naming, excluded destination; delete held, card text, refused missing and folder paths, allowed once, declined). Checked end to end in the browser with a stub model on a Studio with no platform connection: the move ran, the card listed both files, and they were deleted only after Yes. HELP and README updated.

### fix(chat): opening a file from the chat keeps the reply and the queued messages (#681)

Sending a message with an image while a reply streamed queued it, and opening the image from the chat then stopped the reply and dropped the queued message.

Two causes:

- ChatView took any hash other than `#chat=<id>` as "no conversation". Opening an attachment or file navigates to `#open=...`, which closed the conversation, aborted the stream and cleared the queue. Only the chat's own hashes, or an empty hash, change the conversation now.
- The chat stays mounted (hidden) while another page shows, and @parallelworks/ui's SessionView keeps a window Escape listener that stops the turn. Escape that closed the viewer stopped the reply. A pnpm patch of @parallelworks/ui 0.120.0 has it stop only while the view is on screen (has layout and is not visibility hidden). The same change goes upstream; the patch is dropped on the release that carries it.

Verified in a local Studio against a slow stub model: send, attach an image and queue a second message, open the image from the queued message, press Escape in the Library, return to the chat. Before: the stream was cancelled and the queued message never sent. After: both replies complete and the conversation is still open. Web typecheck and tests pass; HELP.md describes the queue and Escape behavior.

### Viewer: PDF pages show as separate sheets; a shorter PDF no longer requests missing pages (#682)

The Pages view showed the server-rendered page images edge to edge with no styling, white on the white viewer, so page edges, margins and page breaks were invisible.

- `.pdf-pages` is now a column on the muted panel color (`--theme-muted-panel-bg`, light and dark) with 16px padding and a 16px gap.
- Each page (server image or pdf.js canvas) is white with a light shadow and hairline edge, up to 1100px wide.
- A page image not loaded yet takes a letter page's shape (`aspect-ratio: auto 17 / 22`), so the lazy-loaded pages below the fold have height and load as they scroll in, then take their own shape.

Checked in Chromium and WebKit, light and dark, with a three-page PDF. Web tests pass. HELP.md describes the view.

Also fixed here: PagedPreview stayed mounted from one file to the next, so the first render of the new file used the previous file's page count and requested pages that do not exist. Server logs show this as "page render failed: Wrong page range given: the first page (N) can not be after the last page (M)", and the late errors could switch the new file to the pdf.js fallback. The preview is now keyed by the file. Checked by opening a three-page PDF and then a one-page PDF: before, page 2 of the one-page file was requested and failed with 500; after, only page 1 is requested.

### Library: a raw HTML or SVG file opened as a page runs no script (#684)

`GET /api/kb/raw` served library files inline as their own Content-Type with no CSP and no `nosniff`. An `.html` or `.svg` file opened at that URL, as a page in a tab or through a link in a chat reply, ran its scripts on the Studio's origin with the user's session. The file could be in the library, uploaded, or written by the chat. Those scripts could call the Studio's APIs as that user.

- `raw` now sends `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on every file.
- HTML, SVG, XHTML and XML get `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox; default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:`: an opaque origin with no scripts.
- The policy binds only a document. An SVG or PNG in an `<img>` and a PDF fetched by pdf.js are unchanged, and PDFs, images and other types get no CSP, so a PDF opened in a tab still shows in the browser's viewer.
- Chat attachment downloads also send `nosniff`.
- `/api/kb/html` is unchanged. It is still the route that runs a page's inline scripts, sandboxed.

Test: `internal/kb/raw_sandbox_test.go` checks the headers for HTML, SVG, PDF, PNG and an unknown type whose body looks like HTML.

### Reports: PDF and Word files embed the images their Markdown names (#683)

A screenshot named in a report's Markdown did not appear in the PDF: `write_kb_file` rendered .pdf and .docx from text only and printed an image as `[alt]`.

- **Parsing** (`docwrite/blocks.go`): `![alt](src)` in a paragraph becomes an image block where it stands, and the paragraph is split around it. In a heading or table cell it stays as `[alt]` text.
- **Loading** (`docwrite/images.go`): each image is read once through an `ImageSource` and checked with `image.DecodeConfig`. A JPEG embeds as it came. PNG, GIF, WebP, BMP and TIFF are redrawn as 8-bit PNG, and a CMYK JPEG as RGB JPEG, so both writers take them. Limits are 25 MB and 50 megapixels per image, and 100 images per document.
- **PDF:** each image is drawn at 96 pixels per inch, scaled down to the text width and to one page's height, and moved to a new page when it does not fit below. Each image is stored once in the file however often it appears.
- **Word:** each image is an inline picture in a `word/media` part with an image relationship, sized in EMU to the same limits. Media entries are deflated: LibreOffice refuses a package whose stored entries carry Go's data descriptor (found while checking; there is a test for it).
- **Resolving** (`chat/docimages.go`): a path relative to the new file's folder, then from the library's top. A leading slash, `#open=file:…`, `/api/kb/raw?path=…` and URL-escaped paths are accepted, and so is a base64 `data:` URL. Excluded and dot folders and paths leaving the library are refused. Web images are not fetched.
- **Reporting:** the tool result says "with N images". It lists each image that was not embedded and why, and asks the model to fix the path and write the file again. That image's alt text stands in its place, in italics.
- **Docs:** the tool description, HELP.md and README say images are supported.

Tests:
- `docwrite/images_test.go`: parsing and splitting, PDF image objects, Word media, relationships, extents scaled to 6.5 in, deflated entries, missing images, a nil source.
- `chat/docimages_test.go`: every reference form and refusal, plus `write_kb_file` end to end.

Checked by eye: a PDF with a screenshot, rendered with poppler, and the Word file converted by LibreOffice.

Also: PDF italics came out upright where only `fonts-dejavu-core` provides DejaVu (the container), because that package has no oblique faces and missing faces were drawn from the regular one. The writer now picks a family with all four faces first (Liberation, also installed there) and falls back to a partial family only when none is complete. Checked on a host with the same font packages.

## v1.196 (2026-11-12)

### Chat: no blank space under the composer from screen reader labels (#677)

A screen reader label (a link's "opens in new tab" text) inside a clipped block of an answer was positioned against the chat thread, escaped the clip, and stretched the thread's scroll height far past the composer. Opening such a chat, or Jump to latest, scrolled into blank space.

The labels in the thread are now pinned to the top of their containing block, so they add no scroll height.

Verified in WebKit and Chromium with a clipped block holding a link: scroll height 6016 against a composer bottom of 2541 before, equal after.

### Code: list pw code sessions on the platform and link to them (#675)

A **Code** page (Run group, shown only with a platform connection, like Workflows) for PW Code on the web:

- Lists the viewer's pw code sessions across the platform's machines, the same list as the platform's Code page: waiting for you, working, recent, and archived behind **Show archived**; pinned first; filter by title, machine, folder, model or branch. A line names the machines whose pw code daemon is running.
- Choosing a session shows its conversation read only (user messages, replies as Markdown, each tool call on one line with its result folded under it), opened at the latest messages and refreshed every 5 s while it works. Status, machine, folder, model, branch and pull requests head it.
- **Open in ACTIVATE** opens `/code/<machine id>/<session id>` on the platform; **New session in ACTIVATE** opens its Code page.

Server: `internal/codesessions` serves `GET /api/code-sessions` and `GET /api/code-sessions/item`, reading the platform's `/api/code/sessions` and `/api/code/machines/{m}/sessions/{id}` as the viewer with the run pane's credential. History is trimmed (latest 400 items, no thinking or turn markers, tool results cut to 1,500 characters). A 403, or a 404 on the list, is explained as the agents preview being off. Read only by design: the platform's start, message, approve and stop routes are internal to its preview; when its client is opened up, the same credential can drive them.

Checked against a live platform (17 sessions, one connected machine): list, detail, links. Tests: grouping, time and path labels, transcript folding (web), title, URL, view and id checks (Go); setup wizard tests updated for the new switch. HELP, README and REFERENCE updated.

## v1.195 (2026-11-12)

### chat: run a prompted tool call written after prose (#672)

Models on the prompted tool format sometimes write a sentence and then the `studio-tools-1` envelope in the same reply. The parser accepted only a reply that was the envelope alone, so the call never ran and the raw JSON showed in the chat.

- `splitEnvelope` finds an envelope inside a reply when it carries this turn's nonce, cuts it (and a markdown fence around it) out of the text, and returns its calls. An envelope without the nonce, such as one quoted from a file, stays text.
- The loop shows the text around the envelope, as it would for a natively calling model, and never shows the envelope itself, even when it names no offered tool.

Tested with unit cases (whole reply, fenced, after a sentence, between paragraphs, foreign nonce, unoffered tool) and end to end against a stub model on the prompted format: the sentence streams, the tool runs, and the answer follows.

### viewer: CSV and TSV files open as a table (#673)

A delimited file used to open on its source text, one long line per row. It now opens on a **Table** tab:

- RFC 4180 parsing (quoted fields, doubled quotes, line breaks inside a field), with the delimiter detected (comma, tab, semicolon, pipe; tab for .tsv).
- Header row and row numbers stay in view; the table scrolls in its own box, sized to the window.
- Columns size to their content; long values wrap at a reading width in their cell.
- Numeric columns are right aligned and sort as numbers; a header click cycles ascending, descending, unsorted.
- **Filter rows** keeps rows holding its text; rows are drawn 500 at a time with **Show more**.
- A preview cut at the 512 KB limit drops the half row and says so. **Source** keeps the file as written.

Tests: parser, delimiter detection, truncation, sort and filter (web suite 509 pass). Checked in the browser on a 1,300 row file. HELP and README updated.

### chat: write PDF, Word and Excel files (#674)

`write_kb_file` wrote text only, so asking the chat to save a report as a PDF got an explanation instead of a file. Now:

- **.pdf / .docx**: made from the Markdown the model writes as `content`: headings, bold, italic, strike, code, web links (Studio-internal links keep their text), nested bulleted and numbered lists (each numbered list restarts at its own start), tables (column widths from content, numeric columns right aligned, header repeated across pages), block quotes, code blocks, rules. PDF is US Letter with 1 inch margins and page numbers; Word uses Calibri with real Heading 1-4 styles, a fixed table grid, and hyperlinks.
- **.xlsx**: rows from CSV/TSV, Markdown tables (one sheet each, named by the heading above it), or JSON `{"sheets":[{"name":..,"rows":[[..]]}]}` (also a bare array of rows or of objects). Numbers become numbers (codes with leading zeros stay text), a value starting with `=` is a formula, the first row is bold, frozen and filterable, columns sized to content.
- **.pptx, .doc, .xls, .odt** and similar are refused with what to write instead.
- The tool description tells the model all this, so it stops saying it can only write text.

New package `internal/docwrite`. Dependencies: `github.com/yuin/goldmark` v1.8.7 (MIT, was already indirect), `github.com/go-pdf/fpdf` v0.9.0 (MIT; the project is no longer developed but is stable and pure Go), and `excelize` promoted from indirect. The PDF embeds the first complete TrueType family on the host (DejaVu, Liberation, Arial, or `STUDIO_PDF_FONT_DIR`) so non-Latin characters draw; with none it falls back to Helvetica and Courier with a few symbols folded to ASCII.

The Node server's catalog entry for `write_kb_file` is unchanged; Studio runs the Go server, and CI does not run the Node catalog comparison.

Tests: Markdown parsing, PDF output, DOCX parts well formed with the expected styles, numbering and links, XLSX from CSV, Markdown, JSON sheets and objects (types, formulas, sheet names), refusals. Checked end to end through a chat turn with a stub model writing each format, the PDF and the DOCX (via LibreOffice) rendered and inspected, and each file opened in the Library viewer. HELP, README and GO-PORT updated.

## v1.194 (2026-11-12)

### Chat: @ to name library files, reasoning effort, table and copy fixes (#669)

Adds two composer features and fixes four chat problems.

**@ library files.** Typing @ in the composer lists the chat library's top folder, narrows by file name as you type (the index's name search, or the folder's listing where a library has no index), opens a folder in place, and writes a chosen file as `@[path]` (or `@[library:path]` for another library). Before the first model call the server reads each named file's index text as `read_kb_file` would for the reader, and puts it in that turn's system prompt (up to 8 files, 16,000 characters between them). In sent messages the tokens are drawn as links with the CSS Custom Highlight API, leaving the package's DOM alone, and a click opens the file.

**Effort.** A Default / Low / Medium / High / Max control beside the model, kept per conversation in the browser, sent as `effort` on `/api/chat/stream`. The server passes it as `reasoning_effort` (which the ACTIVATE gateway takes and validates), or through a model's `chatTemplateKwargs` entry: gpt-oss's `reasoning_effort` (capped at high) and Qwen's `enable_thinking`. A provider that refuses it gets the turn again without it, and that model skips it until restart.

**Fixes**
- Table cells broke paths and words anywhere (`word-break: break-all` from #645). Links and inline code now carry `<wbr>` after `/ _ . -`, so a path wraps between its parts and words stay whole; headers wrap between words, so a five-column table fits the reading column instead of pushing its last column out of view.
- Copy buttons failed in a frame without clipboard access ("Couldn't copy pw code command"). `navigator.clipboard.writeText` now falls back to a textarea copy.
- On a touch screen wider than a phone (an iPad), the page could stay panned after the on-screen keyboard closed, stranding the composer mid screen. The phone's no-page-scroll layout now applies to every touch screen, and the page returns to the top when the keyboard closes. Not verified on a real iPad.
- The slash palette took the canvas's full height (`.chat-canvas > *`); palettes are now as tall as their lists.

**Tested**
- Go: `go test ./internal/chat/ ./internal/settings/`, with new tests for mention parsing and the effort mapping and refusal detection.
- Web: the full vitest suite (505 tests, 66 files), with new tests for the @ query, tokens, `<wbr>` breaking, the effort store, and the clipboard fallback.
- End to end in Chromium and WebKit against a scratch Studio and a stand-in model server: the picker lists folders and names; the request carried `reasoning_effort: "high"` and both named files' text; a provider 400 on `reasoning_effort` was retried without it; the token in the sent bubble opened the file; and copy succeeded in a frame where the clipboard API was refused.

## v1.193 (2026-11-11)

### Updates: keep offering Reopen now until the app reopens (#665)

After an update that changed the app's window, the **Updated to** line with **Reopen now** showed once. Dismissing it, or reloading the page, left the offer only in Settings, General, Updates, where it is easy to miss.

Each page load now shows a shorter line, "Reopen to finish updating to vX", with **Reopen now**, while the server reports `reopen`. It does not show beside the announcement, which carries the button itself, nor while the page is asking the app to reopen on its own. Dismissing it hides it until the next load. It goes as soon as a status read reports `reopen` false, and a hosted deployment never shows it.

Tests in `web/test/updateNotice.test.tsx` cover the dismissed and already seen cases, Reopen now from the reminder, clearing on `reopen` false, and hosted. HELP.md and REFERENCE.md describe the line.

### Updates: a workflow deployment updates itself from Settings (#666)

A Studio deployed through the ACTIVATE workflow refused updates ("This Studio is updated by its deployment"), so a new version meant relaunching the workflow.

A deployment of a GitHub release now updates from Settings, General, Updates, as the Linux app does: the same check, signed and checksummed download, Roll back, and channel.

**Who.** The workflow sets `STUDIO_UPDATE_OWNERS` from the platform's `PW_USER`. Where sign-in is on, only those usernames get the update routes; anyone else gets the hosted 403 as before. Without sign-in the deployment is one person's.

**Server** (`internal/updates/deployment.go`). With `STUDIO_HOSTED_UPDATES=1` and a replaceable payload, a hosted Studio is mode `app` with `deployment: true`. It never sets `reopen`, treats a `requiresRelaunch` release as a restart, and removes the window files (`bin`, `share`, `install.sh`, `uninstall.sh`) from the new copy, as the workflow does.

**Workflow.**
- The server runs under `studio-serve.sh` in the workdir. Exit 75 and 76 start it again at once, other stops after a backoff. After an update (`pending.json`), three stops within two minutes put `.payload.previous` back and write `rolled-back.json`, matching the Linux app's run loop.
- `STUDIO_RESTARTABLE=1` is set, since the loop restarts.
- The watchdog stops the loop before the server and looks twice, 30 seconds apart, before acting. The stop step and cleanup sweep the loop.
- A relaunch that follows Stable keeps an updated copy that is not older than Stable. A pinned tag keeps it while the tag is unchanged. Load Latest Bundle replaces it.
- Bucket bundles and containers are unchanged.

**Web.** `deployment` adjusts two messages that told people to reopen the app.

**Tested.**
- `deployment_test.go`: mode gating, owners (case, `user:` prefix, nobody named, no sign-in), and an install of a `requiresRelaunch` release that restarts with 76, leaves no window files, `reopen` or `relaunch.json`, and keeps the previous copy.
- The run loop on its own: a payload that exits at once is rolled back after three stops.
- A real workflow deployment on the ACTIVATE platform, launched from this branch's yaml and pinned to v1.191, with this branch's server swapped in. Signed in through the session proxy, the username matched the owner the workflow recorded. **Update now** downloaded v1.192, swapped it in, and the loop restarted it within seconds. The page reloaded onto v1.192, `.payload.previous` held v1.191, and the new payload had no window files.

Existing deployments pick this up after one relaunch with the updated workflow. Docs: DEPLOY.md, HELP.md, REFERENCE.md.

## v1.192 (2026-11-11)

### Zoom the desktop window with the web view's own page zoom (#663)

The macOS window has zoomed with CSS zoom on the page's body since the move to Wails (v1.190). In WebKit that leaves the pointer, the page's layout and what is drawn apart by the zoom factor. Measured in WebKit at 125%: a More actions button at x 564 opened its menu at x 705, the model and status menus ended at y 946 in a 900 px window, and the library divider moved 125 px for a 100 px drag.

View, Zoom In, Zoom Out and Actual Size now set `WKWebView.pageZoom`, as the Swift window did, so the page lays out at the new size and menus and drags line up at any zoom. The Linux window gets Ctrl+=, Ctrl+- and Ctrl+0 through WebKitGTK's zoom level, which it did not have before. Steps run from 50% to 300%, and the level is kept in `run/window-zoom` for the next launch.

The shim keeps the macOS title row level with the window controls, which do not zoom (at least 36 px so its buttons fit at high zoom), and maps file drops from window points to page pixels.

Tested:
- WebKit (Playwright) against a v1.190.2 server: CSS zoom misplaces every menu and the divider, page zoom places them as at 100%.
- The Linux app built with this shell (Docker, `build_shell.sh wk41`, vet and tests pass) on the VNC desktop: Ctrl+= twice to 125%, the status and Add menus open at their buttons, the library divider follows the cursor, Ctrl+0 and Ctrl+- step as expected, and a relaunch opens at 125%.
- `window_shots.sh` gains a check that zooms the Mac window to 125% and fails unless the page lays out at that size, the body has no CSS zoom, the web view's `pageZoom` is 1.25, and a menu opens at its button inside the window. The checker passes on the page zoom result and fails on the CSS zoom one.

Not yet run on a Mac: the Objective-C side compiles and runs only in the mac-app workflow.
