## v1.190.2 (2026-11-10)

### Keep a root-built index's text to file permissions; share built indexes in library lists (#658)

An administrator can build one index as root and hand it out as a library list, and each person who imports it sees what their own permissions allow. Testing that setup found one leak and a few gaps, fixed here.

**Leak.** GUFI gives each index folder its source folder's owner, group and mode, so anyone who can enter a folder can read its `db.db`, including the Studio's `words` table. A Studio running as root extracted the text of a file whose own mode is narrower than its folder's (a root-only file in an open folder), and anyone who could enter the folder could find its text by search.

- New `internal/posixaccess`: with `STUDIO_TEXT_ACCESS=file`, the default when the Studio runs as root, a file's text (and so its passages and vectors) is written only when everyone who can enter its folder can read it, judged by owner, group and mode. Other files are indexed by name only, and the text phase logs how many. `folder` keeps today's behavior, the default for a Studio running as its own user.
- Under the same setting the extract cache folder is made 0700 and the embedding cache 0600, since they hold the text of every file read and the cache mirrors the source's names.
- A rebuild rewrites each folder's table, so text written before goes when the setting is on.

**Export.** A built library always went into a library list as a folder for each person to index again. **Share the indexes built here** (`shareBuilt`, off by default, shown when a ticked library was built) writes it as an index to connect: `index` for one built here, `ssh` or `pw` in connect mode for one built elsewhere when its index path is known and not in `~/.activate-studio`.

**Smaller fixes.**
- A file system permission refusal answers 403 with "Permission denied: the account the Studio runs as cannot open this." in place of a 500 internal error. The message names no path.
- The Library tree reads its folders again when the set of libraries changes, so an imported or removed library shows without pressing refresh.

**Docs.** ACCESS-CONTROL.md gets an "An administrator's index" section: the two ways to build (a Studio as root, run where no one else can reach it, or GUFI alone), the 777 mode `gufi_dir2index` leaves on the index folder, the hand-out, and the tested result. REFERENCE (Indexing, text and file permissions), LIBRARIES, HELP and README updated.

**Testing.**
- Go: all packages pass; new tests for the permission rule (14 cases), the text pass at file and folder level including the switch both ways, the export option, and the 403.
- Web: 494 tests pass; new test for the export option.
- End to end on Linux with this branch's server: a root-owned share with an open folder, a group folder, a root-only folder, another group's folder, and a root-only file in the open folder. Root built it with the Studio and exported it with the share option; a Studio running as a member of the first group imported it. Search returned the open and group files and only the name of the root-only file; reading any file that user cannot open returned 403. Both servers ran in a private network namespace.

### Linux app: save to ~/Downloads when XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR is the home folder (#659)

xdg-user-dirs writes `XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR="$HOME/"` for a folder that is not set. The Linux shell compared the expanded value to the home folder without its trailing slash, missed it, and saved Export CSV, conversation downloads and library list exports into the home folder itself. Both sides are now cleaned before comparing, so that case falls back to ~/Downloads, and a set folder is cleaned of a trailing slash.

Testing: `TestXDGDownloadDir` covers a set folder, a non-ASCII folder with a trailing slash, an absolute path, `$HOME/`, `$HOME`, an empty value, a file without the key, and no file. The shell package needs GTK to build, so the test was run on the function in a scratch module; Linux shell tests are not run in CI. Found on a Linux desktop whose user-dirs.dirs has `$HOME/`.

## v1.190.1 (2026-11-10)

### Publish the Go version's container image with each release (#655)

Releases published the Node version's image (`deploy/app.def`) to ghcr.io from `container.yaml`. The Go image (`deploy/app-go.def`) was built and smoke-tested in every `linux-app` run but never published, so the workflow's Container option and the compute-node path still ran Node.

## Changes

- `container-go.yml` (new) builds the Go image from a published release's Linux app, checked against its `.sha256`. Its smoke test checks the version, GUFI, the change log, and that a document is found after the index on start. It pushes the image to ghcr.io as `:<release>`, and `:latest` when the release is GitHub's latest. As in `container.yaml`, only the push job holds the packages token, and the image gets a provenance attestation.
- `linux-app.yml`'s release job starts `container-go.yml` once it has attached the Linux app.
- `container.yaml` no longer runs on releases. It still builds and tests the Node image on pull requests, and can publish it by hand.
- The workflow's Container option, `docs/DEPLOY.md`, `deploy/COMPUTE.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/REFERENCE.md` and the README describe the Go image. The parser golden is regenerated with Node for the new tooltip.

## Tested

- Built the image from the v1.190 Linux app with `deploy/app-go.def` (locally with Apptainer 1.3.4, which needs the base image by digest alone; CI's SingularityCE 4.5.1 takes the tag and digest as written).
- On a test resource on the platform, in strict multi-user posture: deployed the published Node v1.188 image in Container mode, seeded a folder, an upload, a label and a conversation, then relaunched the same deployment with the Go image. It served v1.190 with the same index folder, the seeded state carried over, and the same 50 checks as the host-mode test passed (uploads, search by name, words and meaning, previews, PDF pages, rename, copy, move, delete, labels, conversations, settings, semantic map, workflows catalog).
- `container-go.yml` itself can only be dispatched once it is on main. After merging, I will run it for v1.190, which publishes the Go image as `:v1.190` and `:latest`. The Node image build for the v1.190 release was cancelled before it pushed, so `:v1.190` does not exist yet, and `:latest` is the Node v1.188 image until that run.

### Fix two CI flakes: ldconfig's pipe and the search scope test (#654)

Two tests failed once each today with nothing wrong in the code they test.

- `deploy/linux/test_in_container.sh` looked up each library with `ldconfig -p | awk '... exit'`. awk's early exit could send ldconfig SIGPIPE, and under `pipefail` the script then ended with exit 141. That failed the ubuntu:22.04 test of the v1.190 release run once, after every check had passed. awk now reads to the end and prints the first match.
- `web/test/libraryScope.test.tsx` fired its search as soon as the Libraries button was drawn. The search listener is re-registered by that render's effects, which may not have run yet, so on a slow runner the event reached the listener from before the libraries arrived and searched `all` (the macOS job of this PR). The test now lets pending effects run first. In a browser they run within a frame, long before anyone could type a search.

Tested: the scope test passes three runs in a row locally; CI on this PR.

### Document access control: GUFI permissions and per-person deployments (#656)

Adds docs/ACCESS-CONTROL.md, linked from the README, MULTI-USER.md and ARCHITECTURE.md.

It explains how access is decided today: every search, query and assistant tool runs gufi_query as the Studio's account (or the ssh account for a remote library), and GUFI skips index folders that account cannot open. Text in the Studio's own tables is readable per folder. Text in GUFI external databases is readable per file, because each database carries the access of its files and --external-copy leaves out a database the caller cannot open. Checked locally with GUFI 0.8.0: an unreadable ext database in a folder is left out while the readable one answers (exit 0), and an index folder of mode 000 is skipped while the rest of the tree answers.

Deployment guidance: one Studio per person (Mac app, Linux app, or a per-person ACTIVATE session) enforces user and group permissions today, by building per person or by connecting one administrator-built index locally or over ssh (gufi_jail logins work). A shared Studio runs as one account, as MULTI-USER.md already says.

Docs only.

### Export and import library lists (#657)

An administrator can now share one file that sets up libraries in each person's own Studio. A library list is a JSON file (`<label>.studio-libraries.json`, format `activate-studio-libraries`, version 1) of where each library is and how it is built. Each person imports it at setup or in Settings, and each library is added as that person, so their own ssh login and permissions apply.

**Export.** Settings, Indexing, Libraries has **Export…**: the libraries ticked (all but the main folder by default; the main folder only when ticked, as a folder to index), saved as a download the way an exported table is. The file has no ids, build state, counts, build dates, caps, user hashes, keys, tokens, passwords or settings, and no ssh options that name the exporter's key files or ssh config (`-i`, `-F`, `IdentityFile`, `CertificateFile`, `IdentityAgent`). Folders the Studio made in the exporter's home on a remote system (`~/.activate-studio`) are left out and made again on import. **Leave out the user name**, on by default, writes `host` for `user@host` and drops `-l`, `User=` and jump host user names. A library built by the platform's index workflow is left out with a note.

**Import.** **Import…** in Settings, Indexing, Libraries, **Import a library list from a file…** in Add a library, and **Import a library list from your administrator** on setup's Other libraries step take the file, chosen or pasted. The preview lists each entry with its kind, label, where it points and a tick. Entries already present (same index directory or folder, or same host, port and index directory or source folder), unreadable (unknown kind, bad field, newer format version) or not addable here (sign-in rules) show the reason and are unticked. An ssh entry has **Connect as**, prefilled with the login the Studio runs as when the file names none. Each ticked entry is then added through the existing Add a library routes (`POST /api/libraries`, `/api/libraries/build/check` and `/build`, `/api/user-libraries/ssh` and `/pw` and their `/build/test` and `/build`, and `PUT /api/libraries/:id/read-through`), with one result line each: Added, Failed with the reason, or Skipped.

**Server.** New package `server-go/internal/libconfig` with two routes: `POST /api/libraries/export` writes the file, and `POST /api/libraries/import/check` parses, normalizes and checks one. Neither adds a library. `userlibs.Module.OfferedTo` exposes what the viewer may add, as `GET /api/user-libraries` reports it.

**Shared mode.** With sign-in on, `index` and `folder` entries are shown as not addable (libraries on that computer are the deployment's), as are `ssh` entries (ssh is for a Studio with sign-in off); `pw` entries follow the viewer's platform key.

Docs: LIBRARIES.md (new "Library lists" section with the format and rules), HELP.md (Library and setup), REFERENCE.md (routes), ACCESS-CONTROL.md, README.

**Verification**
- Go: `go test -p 4 ./...` passes (59 packages), including new unit tests for parse, normalize, export (no state or key file options leak, user name stripping, primary only when ticked, round trip), duplicates and availability, and an HTTP test of both routes. `scripts/crossvet.sh` clean.
- Web: vitest 65 files, 493 tests (and the rhel9 config, 64 files, 479 tests) pass, with new tests for the import preview and adds, single entry adds, and the export dialog and download.
- End to end with the Go server (Node off): an admin Studio with a GUFI index here, a folder built here, and a GUFI index over ssh to a private sshd on loopback (identity given with `-i`). The export left out the user name and the `-i` option. Imported over HTTP into a fresh Studio (the ssh login authenticating through an agent) and through the UI in another fresh Studio's setup wizard (file chooser, preview, Add 3 libraries: all Added); in both, searches in each of the three libraries returned their files. Settings, Import… on a Studio that already had them showed all three as Already added with Add disabled.

## v1.190 (2026-11-09)

### Deploy the Go version from the ACTIVATE workflow (#652)

The ACTIVATE workflow (`deploy/workflow.yaml`, and the generated `deploy/workflow-cfd-studio.yaml`) now deploys the Go version. Its GitHub and Bundle modes run the Linux app the release ships, `activate-studio-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`: the Go server, the interface, GUFI, tesseract, and the ONNX runtime with the search by meaning model. Nothing is cloned or built on the resource, and it needs no Node or Python.

## Changes

- GitHub release mode downloads the named release's Linux app (`main` means the current Stable release, the fixed `linux` release) and checks it against its `.sha256`. Bundle mode takes the same file from a bucket or a pre-staged copy. A relaunch from the same file keeps the app in place unless Load Latest Bundle is set.
- `deploy/make_bundle.sh` downloads and checks a release's Linux app for upload to a bucket (`--release TAG`), or takes a local build (`--from FILE`).
- A deployment that kept its index, settings and credentials in `app/index` (no Index Directory set) has them moved to `data/index` on its first launch. The Node tree, GUFI build and Node runtime are removed.
- Index on Launch posts `/api/reindex` once the server answers.
- The watchdog restarts a failed server on the same port and leaves the endpoint process running. Before, it re-registered the endpoint as well, which the platform refuses once the workflow run has ended, so the session's address went dead after the first restart. This was also true of v1.188.
- The container and compute-node paths are unchanged and still run the image built from `deploy/app.def`.
- Docs: `docs/DEPLOY.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/REFERENCE.md`.

## Merge order

`main` resolves to the Stable Linux release, which is still v1.188 (the Node payload). The workflow refuses a payload without `app/bin/studio-server`, so a launch with Release set to `main` fails until a Go release is on Stable. Merge this together with the next Stable release.

## Tested

On a test resource on the platform, in strict multi-user posture:

- Upgrade from a v1.188 Node deployment in GitHub mode: the seeded folder, upload, label and conversation carried over. 50 checks passed: uploads (single file, folder, PDF, docx, from a URL), path escape refused, reindex, search by name, words and meaning, extractors, view, download, PDF pages, rename, copy, move, delete, labels, statistics, query, libraries, settings, chat attachment, conversations, model key, semantic map and the workflows catalog.
- Upgrade from a v1.188 Node deployment with no Index Directory, in Bundle mode from a bucket (bundle from `make_bundle.sh --release v1.189`): the index moved to `data/index`, the seeded state carried over, and the same 50 checks passed.
- A personal key stored in the browser cookie by the Go server survived a redeploy and a server restart; the keycookie format matches the Node version (`TestWithNode`).
- Killing the server: the watchdog restarted it on the same port within its two-minute check, and the session address kept working.
- Every run block in both workflows passes `bash -n`.
- Without a personal key, platform calls use the job's own token and the platform API answers 401. The same happens in the Node version.

## v1.189 (2026-11-09)

### The Studio runs as one Go program; the macOS window is built with Wails (#649)

The Studio's server and indexer now run as one Go program, with no Node or Python. The macOS app's window is now built with Wails, the toolkit the Linux app's window already uses. Installed apps update to this version through the usual update: on macOS from v1.141, the first release with a macOS app, and on Linux from v1.187, the first Linux release.

## What changed

The Node server (`server/src`) and the indexer's Python steps (`indexer/`) are ported to Go in `server-go/`. Every route the Node server answered is answered by the Go server, with the same requests, responses and error bodies. The web app is unchanged apart from the features below. The desktop apps ship `app/bin/studio-server` in place of Node, Python and the indexer scripts. On the other systems the Studio builds libraries on, it sends a Go helper in place of Python. Search by meaning still uses ONNX Runtime and the MiniLM model.

On macOS the window is the Wails window (`desktop/wails`) in place of the Swift window. It has no title bar of its own. The window controls sit on the sidebar's first row, with the collapse button at its right end and the icon and name on the row under it; that row is also the row of each column's heading. With a classification banner set, the window takes a plain title bar's height and the banner fills it, with the controls over its left end; the change happens as the banner is turned on or off. An empty part of the top row drags the window, and a double click zooms it. The bundle identifier, app path, data folder and LaunchAgent are the same.

## Updates

No bridge release is needed. The updaters of the installed releases check a new copy for files only, and the Go build carries stand-ins at those paths. After the swap the old run loop starts the new copy's run script, which starts the Go server. Under the run loops of v1.141 to v1.169 on macOS, the stand-in for `node` starts the Go server. If the new version fails to start three times in a row, the run loop puts the previous copy back. This holds until the new version's first clean start. A person still in the old macOS window is offered **Reopen now**, and the old window works until then.

Settings, Updates no longer offers a rollback to a Node release, and **Install a version**, **Move to Stable** and **Roll back** offer only Go releases. A snapshot of the settings, conversations, libraries list and keys is still taken before every change of version.

## Also in this version

- Settings, Indexing is a section under Studio with four tabs: Libraries, Sync and search, Building, and Storage and logs. The Library's **+ Add** menu links to Add a library.
- With AI features off, the settings, pages and status lines that need the assistant are hidden: Assistant tools, Feature previews, Extensions, the Chat and Agents pages and their sidebar switches, image descriptions, and delegation and attached MCP servers under External access. Model access becomes ACTIVATE access. Switching AI features on brings them back without a reload.
- Building a library of a folder on this computer, in Add a library and in setup, offers suggested folders: Documents, Desktop and Downloads, and on macOS Apple Mail's folder, with a link to Full Disk Access, which macOS requires for it. A suggestion fills in the folder and runs the check.
- Apple Mail messages (`.emlx`) and `.eml` files are read at the Text depth and above, searched by meaning on documents, and shown in the file view as the message: subject, sender, recipients, date, body and attachment names.
- Settings, General, Sidebar has a Width choice (Narrow, Default, Wide), and the sidebar's right edge drags from 200 to 400 pixels.
- Branding is part of the Appearance tab.
- The default accent is None, which uses no color. The default surface is Warm gray, a gray with a slight warmth. Neutral gray has no tint.
- In the semantic map, a click on a file selects it. The view moves to the file and shows its nearest files by meaning, with **Open in Library**, which leaves full screen first.
- Ctrl+F (⌘F on a Mac) finds text in the open conversation. The chat uses `@parallelworks/ui` 0.120.0, and the local patch for the chat's scroll position is gone.
- PDFs and Office files of a library on another system preview in the file view.
- PDFs whose pages the server cannot draw, because poppler is not installed (as in the macOS app), are drawn in the viewer by pdf.js; only a PDF neither can draw shows its text.
- The Library tree of a library on another system whose index was rolled up (`gufi_rollup`) lists one folder at a time, where it listed every folder and file below a rolled-up folder at once.
- Indexed text longer than about 60,000 characters shows as plain text, so a long manual's text opens at once: a 90-page manual opened from search in under half a second in the Linux window, where it took about 6 s. Find matches a word across punctuation, as search does, so NIST_SP811 finds "NIST SP811".
- A file that cannot be opened says it may have moved only when it is missing; a file of a library on another system connected without its source directory says to add the library again with that directory.
- Links to a chat's sources open in the right library when all libraries are shown.
- Label suggestions come from the library being edited.
- Test connection fills in a GUFI folder without ".." steps, which Add then accepts.
- The Linux window's title bar takes the page's theme from launch.
- A file opened from a search result opens with Find set to the query only when it was found by its words; one found only by its meaning, name or folder opens without it.
- Where poppler is not installed, as in the macOS app, a PDF's text view says so and gives the command that installs it, in place of an internal error.

## Tested

The Node server and the Go server were run side by side on the same seeded library:
- **Routes:** the Go server serves 219 of the Node server's 221 routes, with the same replies. The two it does not serve are the internal routes between the Go server and a Node server behind it, which the Go version does not run.
- **API:** 75 of 84 parameter-free GET routes answer identically. The other 9 differ only where expected: notes about readers that needed Python, labels with equal counts ordered by name, a folder's time, the port, and the sign-in field.
- **Files:** of 88 file routes, 64 answer identically, and the other 24 differ only in timings and a folder's time.
- **UI:** the side-by-side check of every view found no difference in function.
- **No Python:** an index build at Meaning on documents and a semantic map build, traced on the Go server, started no Python and no Node.

On the release commit: the Go tests, the web tests (487), and the front-end suite run against the Go server in strict mode with every fixture, including a local sshd for libraries on another system (860 pass, 0 fail, 14 skipped). The skips are cases for the Node server's Python readers, which the Go server's own tests cover, and cases that need root or extra Python packages.

The move from the Node releases was run in CI through each old release's own updater, with a throwaway signing key and a local release feed. Each run covered install, data, update to the Go build, data again, and the put-back of a Go build that never starts. On macOS this ran from nine releases between v1.141 and v1.188, each with the old app's own LaunchAgent and, from v1.170, also detached. On Linux it ran from v1.187 and v1.188, on Stable and Preview. All passed.

Twelve rounds on a Linux desktop (WebKitGTK 4.1, real mouse and keyboard) updated the installed app over the air from one Preview to the next and checked the data each time: settings, conversations, libraries, credentials, labels. They covered every view, chat with markdown, previews, remote libraries, Settings and the update path. A scratch v1.188 install also updated to the Go version through its own updater.

On macOS, the CI check runs build, sign with the hardened runtime, run the bridge tests, and take screenshots of the window on a macOS runner in Chat, Library and Settings, in light and dark, with the sidebar expanded and collapsed, with and without a classification banner, and with the banner switched on and off while open. The same window opens a PDF, which pdf.js draws, and builds and searches a library of an Apple Mail folder offered as a suggestion. The Preview releases from v1.188.1 were signed and notarized, and a Mac on the Preview channel updated through them over the air.

## Not tested

Windows under WSL. The macOS app on Intel Macs. It is built for Apple silicon only, as before.

In a WebKit window, find in the conversation leaves earlier matches highlighted as the query grows, until the transcript scrolls. The fix belongs to the shared UI package: parallelworks/foundation#681.

## v1.188 (2026-11-05)

### Linux app runs on RHEL 8 and its rebuilds (#647)

The Linux app now runs on RHEL 8 and its rebuilds, as well as RHEL 9, Ubuntu 22.04 and later. It needed glibc 2.34 before, so GUFI and tesseract failed to load on RHEL 8 and indexing failed there.

## What changed

GUFI, tesseract and the WebKitGTK 4.0 shell are built on Rocky Linux 8. GCC 8 and Python 3.6 are too old for GUFI and tesseract, so on RHEL 8 the build scripts install `gcc-toolset-13` and Python 3.11 (`el8_tools` in `deploy/common/lib.sh`). gcc-toolset links what it adds to the C++ runtime statically, so the binaries still need only the system's libstdc++.

The tree is limited to glibc 2.28, libstdc++ 3.4.25 and CXXABI 1.3.11, in `build_app.sh`, `check_app.sh` and the `.rpm` dependencies. The update manifest's `minGlibc` follows from the tree. The WebKitGTK 4.1 shell still builds on Ubuntu 22.04 and needs glibc 2.35. It is used only where WebKitGTK 4.1 is installed, which RHEL 8 does not have.

`install.sh` and `uninstall.sh` use a glob for the icons, so they no longer need `find`. The Rocky 8 container images leave out findutils.

`README.md` and `docs/LINUX-APP.md` state the new requirements, and the README line that said test builds only is gone, since the Linux app was released in v1.187.

## Tested

A full `linux-app.yml` run on this branch passed every job, with nothing published. Rocky Linux 8 (8.9 and current), AlmaLinux 8, and the existing Rocky 9, AlmaLinux 9 and Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 images ran the payload checks and the update path. The tarball and `.rpm` were installed on Rocky 8 and AlmaLinux 8 and started under Xvfb, where the Studio drew, a search found a document, and uninstall left only the data. The same install tests passed on Rocky 9, AlmaLinux 9 and Ubuntu, so one payload built on the older system runs on all of them.

## Wider coverage

The payload test matrix adds stock RHEL 8 and 9 (UBI images), Oracle Linux 8 and 9, CentOS Stream 9, Fedora 43, Amazon Linux 2023, Ubuntu 20.04 and Debian 11, 12 and 13, and the install test adds Oracle Linux 8 and Debian 12. All passed the 87 payload checks locally.

The build also ran on a remote desktop, driven with real mouse and keyboard input, on Ubuntu 24.04 and on Rocky 8 in a container: window, indexing, search with OCR and meaning hits, query and Stats. The window also opened on Debian 12 and 13, Ubuntu 20.04, Oracle Linux 8 and 9, CentOS Stream 9 and Fedora 43.

## Not tested

A physical Rocky 8 desktop, and the window on stock RHEL (UBI repositories have no WebKitGTK), Debian 11 (its WebKitGTK packages are gone from the mirrors) and Amazon Linux 2023. Chat in the window was not run in this round. On Fedora 43 the window crashed at launch twice in about ten launches and opened on the next try. The cause is not known and is recorded in `docs/LINUX-APP.md`.

## v1.187 (2026-11-05)

### Offer a rebuild when a remote library's depth changes (#635)

Changing the depth of a library built on a remote system used to store the change with a short message, and nothing ran until someone pressed Rebuild. The row now offers **Rebuild now** or **Later** in place, over ssh and pw ssh alike. Libraries built on this computer behave as before.

The choice says what a rebuild does: the current index keeps answering searches until the new one replaces it, and what the new depth costs in time. For a lower depth it says search keeps working without a rebuild. With a build running it says the change applies to the next build and offers no rebuild. Going back to the depth the index already has asks nothing.

A library now records the depth of its last build that finished with what that depth makes (`builtDepth`). Until that matches its depth, the state column says **Depth changed, Rebuild to apply**, also after Later, after closing the page, and after a failed rebuild. A library last built by an earlier version has no record and shows no note until its next build. A build at a Meaning depth that finished without vectors does not count as applied, so the note stays.

Two changes to the remote build come with this. The new index used to be moved into place right after `gufi_dir2index`, before its text and vectors were made, so a library's words and meaning were missing from search while the rest of the build ran, and a build stopped then left an index without them. Text and vectors are now made in the staged tree and it is swapped in at the end, which is what the prompt says and what a library built here already does. The index folder therefore holds two copies for the whole build, not only the folders phase. `embed.py` also gets `--cache "$idx/.embed-cache.db" --prune`, so a rebuild embeds only passages it has not embedded before.

A rebuild still walks and indexes every folder and writes the text tables again. It reuses extracted text from `.extract`. There is no pass that adds meaning alone, which would be the better answer for adding meaning to a large library, and that is left for later.

Tested with web and server tests, and end to end against a throwaway container over ssh and through a stand-in `pw` that forwards to ssh: Text + OCR to Meaning on all files, Rebuild now, words searched during the build, and a search by meaning finding its passage afterwards.

### Read PDFs in remote builds and say what a build could not read (#638)

## Problem

On a remote library, PDFs could be missing from search, chat and the semantic map while the build reported success. `enrich.py` reads PDFs with pdftotext, then pypdf, and returns no text if neither is there. A remote host got pypdf only if it was already installed, and downmark's binary is not on the remote. The library row still showed text and vectors as present.

## Evidence

Real ssh builds against local sshd stand-in hosts, public PDFs, rows counted in each `db.db`. Three text PDFs per host.

| Host | Before: PDF words / gvec rows | After one Rebuild: PDF words / gvec rows | Row after |
|---|---|---|---|
| pdftotext, no pypdf | 3 / 36 | 3 / 36 | Ready |
| Neither reader | 0 / 0, row said text and vectors | 3 / 33 | Ready |
| No Python | 0 / 0, no reason given | 0 / 0 | Says why |
| No Python, then installed | not applicable | 3 / 33 | Ready |
| Python 3.10, neither reader (first build on the new code) | not measured | 3 / 0 | Says no embedding model for this Python |

## Changes

- `embed_deps.json` pins pypdf 6.21.2 (the macOS app's version) and typing_extensions, which pypdf needs on Python 3.10.
- The Studio sends the readers to `~/.activate-studio/readers/<digest>` at every depth with text. `fetch_embed.py` checks each hash and installs with no network on the host.
- `enrich.py` and `embed.py` take `--report`. `.studio-index.json` records those reports, the reasons a pass did not run, and counts from `gufi_query` on the finished index.
- The library row shows "Ready; some files were not read" with the count and reason, such as "312 PDFs have no text: this system has no PDF reader".
- A library whose vector tables are empty although passages were cut now counts as having no vectors.
- A Rebuild reads the system's Python and GGUF model again. Text already read stays in `.extract`.
- pypdf stops after 180 seconds per file and keeps the pages read by then, matching the pdftotext timeout. A single page that hangs is not interrupted.
- A file name search with an underscore now matches. `NIST_SP811` was reduced to `NISTSP811`. This applies to every library.
- The macOS app now carries the reader wheels to send.

## Tests

- New `server/test/remotePdfSshd.test.mjs`: 6 cases over real sshd. It needs `STUDIO_TEST_SSHD=1`, so CI skips it.
- Unit tests that run in CI: row wording, vector check, reader pins, the `enrich.py` report with no reader, the underscore clause, and the row in the web page.
- One existing test changed: `fetch_embed.py` is now sent at Text + OCR because it installs the readers. `embed.py` and `embed_onnx.py` are still not sent there, and the Names depth sends none of them.

## Not tested

- macOS app build with the new wheels step, and a macOS remote host.
- pw ssh with real readers. The real ssh test uses plain ssh.
- Python older than 3.10 as a real interpreter. It takes the same path as no Python.
- A GUFI without sqlite-vec on a real host. The vector check has unit tests only.
- Chat as a live model conversation. Search, which its tool calls, was tested.

## Overlap with #635

A trial merge with `depth-rebuild-prompt` conflicts in `server/src/remoteBuild.ts`, `server/src/userLibraries.ts`, `web/src/api.ts`, `web/src/components/LibrariesSection.tsx` and `docs/HELP.md`. The hunks are adjacent additions, and each resolves by keeping both sides:

- `remoteBuild.ts`: the header comment, and the enrich and embed lines, which need both `--index "$new"` and `--report`, and both `--cache` and `--report`. The tree swap goes after this change's `vecwhy` block. The index counts here run after the swap on `$tree`, so they stay correct.
- `userLibraries.ts`: the `gaps` and `builtDepth` fields, `rebuildRemote`, `finishBuild`, and `publicUserLibrary`.
- `LibrariesSection.tsx`: the row's `notes` line.

One point a textual merge does not catch: `madeDepth` in #635 reads `m.vectors === true`. After the rebase it should call `vectorsMade(m)`, so an empty vector table does not count as the depth being built.

This branch does not add `RemoteBuild.depth`. The build script writes the depth into the manifest instead.

### Chat tool calls fold again, library picker in full screen maps, shorter GUFI commands, chat stays in place (#637)

Four fixes from testing v1.186 on a Mac.

## Tool calls fold again

Since #618 the chat passed `toolRenderers` for `search_kb`, `query_corpus`, `list_kb_dir` and `read_kb_file`. The package keeps a tool with a renderer out of the "Ran N tools" row unless it also has a presentation, and draws each call even when a run of them is folded. These tools now have a `toolPresentation`, so finished calls fold with the rest. The commands and the result summary are inside the call's row. A running call and a failed call keep their own rows. `read_original` has no renderer and already folded.

One limit from the package: a failed call directly beside a finished call of the same tool joins a folded row that counts it ("1 failed"). The reason is one click away there.

## Library picker in the full screen maps

Both maps show the picker in the full screen header. Choosing a library changes the map in place. The window stays open while a library loads and for a library with no map, which shows its reason and its actions. The choice is remembered as before. Escape with the list open closes the list only. The full screen semantic map also shows a remote library's Refresh and notes.

## Shorter GUFI commands

The query vector is shown as `X'3f2a1b0c…' (384-value query vector)`, and the shell's `'\''` escapes read as plain quotes. One line under the commands says what changed on screen. Copy still gives the full command, and the server and the command log are unchanged. A real search by meaning went from 14,982 characters to 5,287 on screen. The copied command ran in bash with exit 0.

## Chat lifting

The thread was not positioned, so its absolutely placed screen reader labels escaped it and gave every box around it the conversation's full height to scroll. In a window of 760 px or less, the package's drawer layout adds an `overflow-hidden` box that was not in the shell list, and a `scrollIntoView` scrolled it 36 px, which left the composer lifted. This reproduces in Chromium and WebKit, on 0.89 and on 0.114.1.

- The thread is now `position: relative`, which removes the extra height (`.chat-canvas` scrollHeight went from 48,607 to 800).
- The drawer box is `overflow: clip`.
- The scroll guard, moved to `shellScroll.ts`, covers every box around the thread.
- The thread has `overscroll-behavior: none`, because the composer sits inside it and macOS elastic scrolling would move the composer with it.

The elastic scrolling change is not verified: Linux WebKit has no rubber band, so this needs a check on a Mac.

## Tests

New vitest coverage for each fix, including `web/test/shellScroll.test.ts`. Web suite: 375 passed. Checked in Chromium and WebKit against a local server, including a live streamed chat with many tool calls and a reload.

Takes `@parallelworks/ui` from ^0.89.0 to ^0.114.1 and uses what the releases added. Closes #580.

Status displays now use the package components. Settings, Agents, Workflows and the status panel use `StatusLabel` and `RunStatusLabel`, and a new `web/src/statusLook.ts` holds the one mapping from a state to its look: under way is blue with a pulse, done is green, failed is red, needs a look is amber, waiting or off is gray. Before this change working and idle were green, completed was gray, and failed was amber in some places. `StatusBadge` is kept for flags only, as the package now requires.

### Update test waits for its restart call before ending (#640)

The macOS job failed twice on main at 41130db in `where the app started its run loop itself`, which checks that no `launchctl kickstart` ran.

The test before it ends with an install and does not wait for that install's restart. The restart is a separate process, so its call can land in the next test's log after `fresh()` clears it. Slowing the fake `launchctl` by 0.15 seconds reproduces the failure on Linux every time.

The earlier test now waits for its kickstart before ending. With the fix, the updater tests pass 22 of 22 in three runs with the slowed fake and three with the normal one. Test only, no change to the app.

### Labels apply to the whole selection and show up everywhere at once (#642)

Multi-select could not apply a label that one selected item already held, because the panel treated a label on any item as a label on all of them. The panel now counts how many selected items hold each label. A label on some of them appears in a new "On some of these items" row with an "n of N" button that adds it to the rest.

The Labels toggle did nothing in select mode, because select mode forced labels on. Select mode now turns the toggle on visibly, and the toggle works from there.

Chat, Search and Overview loaded the label list once, so new labels were missing until a refresh. They now share `useLabelVocabulary`, which reloads on `ade-tags-changed`, and the panel sends that event itself.

Checked in the packaged Linux window on a desktop session. 391 web tests pass and `tsc` is clean. `docs/HELP.md` is updated.

### Uploads keep folders, run side by side, and delete in the background (#643)

Testing the Linux app on a real desktop, plus a drop of nested folders from a laptop, found these. Each was reproduced and rechecked in the packaged window, driven with real input.

**Uploads**
- Nested folders no longer flatten, on any platform. The multipart parser cuts a filename to its base name, so `paths` now goes as a JSON field ahead of the files.
- Each upload, move, copy and delete has its own row (`transfers.ts`, `TransferPanel.tsx`). Uploads take turns, a queued one can be cancelled, and rows outlive a trip to another page.
- The tree updates when files land, and clean rows go by themselves. Failed rows stay.
- A file over 200 MB is named as failed with the reason, and the rest of the upload goes on. Before, one such file failed its whole batch.

**Deletes**
- Bulk and folder delete run as jobs, so the dialog closes at once.
- A deleted folder leaves the Stats count straight away; the cached count used to hold for ten minutes.

**Library and layout**
- Eye button for hidden files, and Choose a folder in + Add.
- Full screen maps clear the title bar in a window controls overlay, and the classification banner.
- The Status panel starts closed under 1200 px, without changing the remembered choice.
- The viewer header wraps in a narrow pane.

**Desktop window**
- `onShellDrop` and `chooseUpload` take drops and folders from the Linux shell, which sends the bytes. The shell half is in #633.
- A drop nothing accepts no longer navigates the window away.

**Labels and details**
- An overlay entry only applies while its path still holds that object, which stops starter labels reaching other files.
- Details says a file has no text only when that is known.

Tests: web 397 passed, server 784 passed and 26 skipped, `tsc` clean. New tests cover upload paths, hidden files, transfers, queued cancel, and the size limit.

### A finished reply keeps the bottom of the chat in view in WebKit (#644)

WebKit has no scroll anchoring. When a finished reply swaps in, the list collapses for a frame, and the late scroll event reads as the reader scrolling up, so the end of the reply stayed below the fold. The macOS and Linux windows are both WebKit, which is why browsers never showed it.

The fix belongs in `ChatMessageList` and is in foundation PR parallelworks/foundation#647. This carries it as a pnpm patch on `@parallelworks/ui` 0.114.1 so the Linux release does not wait on a foundation version. The next `@parallelworks/ui` taken drops the patch, as `pnpm-workspace.yaml` notes.

`patches/*` now counts as an image input in `container.yaml`.

Reproduced in the packaged Linux window and rechecked there: the reply ends at the bottom with its sources and footer in view. Web tests: 397 passed.

### Chat tables show in full and keep their columns in view (#645)

A starter question ("Which PDFs do I have") gives a reply with long tables, and they rendered badly at every width.

- Streamdown caps a table's box with an inline height, so a table was cut off mid row behind its own scrollbar. The cap is gone in chat, and a reply scrolls with the chat. `StepSummaries` in `@parallelworks/ui` makes the same override.
- A long path held its column at full width and pushed the next column out of view. Links and code in a cell now break anywhere. `overflow-wrap` does not reach WebKit's table sizing, so this uses `word-break`.

Checked in the packaged Linux window at 1000 and 1500 px wide.

## v1.186 (2026-11-03)

### fix(web): fall back to plain number formatting when Intl cannot build it (#626)

The WebKitGTK 4.0 packages in RHEL 9 and its rebuilds (Rocky Linux 9.8 and AlmaLinux 9 with webkit2gtk3 2.54.x, Red Hat UBI 9's webkit2gtk3-jsc, all on ICU 67) cannot build an `Intl.NumberFormat` or an `Intl.PluralRules`: every construction throws "failed to initialize", `toLocaleString` on a number aborts the engine, and `Intl.ListFormat` does not exist. The UI library builds these while the bundle loads, so the page stays on its loading screen.

An inline script in `web/index.html`, ahead of the bundle, checks that each of the three can be built. For each one that cannot, it installs a plain English stand-in: `Intl.NumberFormat` (decimal, percent, currency, compact, fraction and grouping options) with `Number` and `BigInt` `toLocaleString`, `Intl.PluralRules` (cardinal and ordinal English rules) and `Intl.ListFormat`. Where the three work, nothing is replaced. Date formatting, collation, relative time and display names work on these engines and are not touched.

## Regression protection

`web/test/intlGuard.test.ts` runs the shipped script (taken out of `index.html`) against an engine whose `Intl.NumberFormat`, `Intl.PluralRules` and `toLocaleString` throw and whose `Intl.ListFormat` is missing, and checks the formatted values. It also loads every module under `web/src` and the packages the page loads late (`@parallelworks/ui`, the workflow parser, `streamdown`, `three`, `yaml`, `react-hook-form`, `monaco-editor`) on that engine with the guard in place, and shows that the app fails to load on it without the guard.

`pnpm test` in `web/` now runs the whole suite twice. The second pass (`web/vitest.rhel9.config.ts`) applies the same broken Intl and then the guard before every test file, as the page does, so every view the tests render is rendered on that engine. A module that builds an Intl formatter at load time which the guard does not replace, or a view that formats a number through something the stand-in lacks, fails there and passes in the first pass. Two mutations were tried to confirm it fails: removing the PluralRules stand-in from the guard fails 3 tests, and a module-scope `new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US').formatRange(1, 5)` fails the module-load test. The second pass adds about 12 s to the suite and needs no container, display or WebKit.

A Rocky 9 job in CI was considered and not added: it needs GUFI built in the job to have a populated index (minutes), plus a display server and WebKitGTK, and it only sees the views it is told to open. The simulated engine reproduces what was measured on the real one (the three failing classes, and nothing else failing).

## Checked on RHEL 9 engines

Every main view was opened in a WebKitGTK 4.0 window (webkit2gtk3 2.54.2 on Rocky Linux 9.8, 2.54.1 on AlmaLinux 9.8, ICU 67.1) under Xvfb against a seeded Studio (a few hundred files, a built index with embeddings, 1,345 files in all so counts have thousands separators). In both, all 22 steps passed with no page errors, no web process crash and no unformatted numbers (`NaN`, `undefined`, `[object`, mis-grouped digits):

Setup wizard (all eight steps), Chat (a streamed reply with a table, list and code block, and a reply after a search tool call, against a stand-in model endpoint), Search with results, Query (a preset run, 50 rows), Stats (counts, sizes and bars; topology map; semantic map in 2D and in 3D, which is drawn on a 2D canvas, and turned), Settings (General, Libraries, Assistant tools, Feature previews, Extensions, External access), Library, the file viewer on Markdown, CSV, PDF, Word and an image, the 3D model viewer (the only WebGL view; it drew an STL with WebGL 2 on software rendering), History, Agents and Help.

Without the guard, the same window stays on the loading screen (the app never mounts), and a `toLocaleString` call from a script then crashes the web process.

Limits: the window is a plain WebKitGTK 4.0 web view, not the Wails shell (the shell's self test drew the first screen earlier); WebGL ran on software rendering; only English formatting was checked; stock RHEL 9 itself was not run (UBI 9 carries the same build); RHEL 8 was not tested.

`tsc --noEmit` passes, and the web suite passes in both passes (44 files, 360 tests, then 43 files, 346 tests). The long-running import tests now have a 60 s timeout: at the 5 s default the app load test timed out once under the parallel run.

## v1.185 (2026-11-03)

### feat(chat): read_original, and a host to read a library's originals through (#629)

## What was missing

The assistant had one tool, `read_kb_file`, that did two jobs. It opened the original file first (on this computer, or over ssh on the library's host) and used the text in the index only when that failed, and only for documents and images. On a site where the index lives on a host whose login runs only `gufi_query`, and another host (a file transfer host that mounts every file system) has the files, a plain text file could not be read at all, and there was no way to tell the Studio where the files are.

## What changed

Reading is split in three, and the tool descriptions and the system prompt say which to use:

- `search_kb` searches, as before.
- `read_kb_file` returns the text the index holds for a file and works whenever the index can be read, with the original out of reach. Each result opens with a line naming its source, for example `[source: index; it can lag behind the file]`. When the index holds no text it says so plainly.
- `read_original` (new) opens the original file: at the library's own location first (this computer, or over ssh on the library's host), then on a host the library names for reading originals. It returns plain text as it is and the extracted text the Studio keeps for documents and images on this computer. When no host can give the file, the message names every host tried and what each said. It takes `path`, `paths` (up to 25), `offset` and `library`, as `read_kb_file` does, and is offered over MCP too.

What `read_kb_file` returns for a plain text file: the index does hold it. The Studio's text pass (`indexer/enrich.py`) stores each text file's contents, up to 500,000 characters, in the `words` table, but only when the library was indexed with text, only for the file types that pass reads, and only as of the last index update. So `read_kb_file` returns the index's text for a plain text file when there is a row, labeled as from the index (and, when the row is at the 500,000 character limit, labeled as possibly cut). Where the index has no text for it, the original is read as before and the source line says so. Documents and images keep their order, except that the original is no longer needed: the index, then the library's extraction cache (a library here), then the original only to explain why there is no text.

The host is a per-library setting, "Read originals through": Settings, Libraries, **Originals via**, **Set**. It takes `user@host` or a Host alias from `~/.ssh/config`, an optional folder (the library's root on that host when the path differs) and optional ssh options. **Test connection** checks ssh, that the login gives a shell, and that the folder is readable; **Save** needs a passing test. It is stored with the library's other settings (`libraries.json`, or the user's library entry for a library over ssh or pw ssh), and a library in `STUDIO_LIBRARIES` can carry it too. The viewer's file text and download use the same two places in the same order.

Safety: the host is held to a destination ssh cannot read as an option (no leading `-`, no whitespace or shell characters), the options to what libraries over ssh already allow, and the folder to an absolute path with no `..`. A file's path is never read by a shell on either side: it goes to the host as an argument of a script, after the existing checks (no `..`, under the library's folder). It uses the same ssh machinery as the libraries over ssh (the account's keys and `~/.ssh/config`, no prompts, a shared connection, bounded waits), so it is offered only on a Studio with sign-in off, and a saved host is not used where sign-in is on. A host whose login runs only `gufi_query` is refused by the test and named in the error when a read reaches it.

`read_kb_file` keeps its name and arguments, so existing conversations that call it work. Its results now begin with the source line.

## Not included

The previews that read a file from this computer (images in the page, PDF pages, Office rendering) are not offered for a file that exists only on the other host. The file text and Download are.

## How it was checked

## v1.184 (2026-11-02)

### feat(gufi): move to GUFI 0.8.0 (#627)

Moves the Studio to GUFI 0.8.0 (tag `0.8.0`, commit `021a717a`) without rebuilding or migrating any index.

## What was measured

GUFI 0.8.0 changed the schema twice: `rollupscore` became `canrollup` and `isrolledup` (June 2026, before this repository's first release, so no Studio build ever wrote `rollupscore`), and `entries`, `summary` and `pentries_rollup` gained a `dev` column (third position). A GUFI maintainer said old indexes do not work with the new code. Measured with 0.8.0 built in user space against indexes written by the commit the macOS app pinned (`1713537a`), by the 0.7.0 tag, and by 0.8.0, in both directions:

- Every query the Studio runs gives the same rows on an old index with 0.8.0 tools, and on a 0.8.0 index with the old tools: the one-pass search walk, Query (builder, canned, SQL), statistics, `gufi_sqlite3`, `gufi_vt`, words, meaning, external `ext.db` tables, labels, history, the semantic map. 0.8.0's views name columns with `.*` and the Studio never reads `dev`.
- What fails is raw SQL that names `dev` (`Error: no such column: dev: <index>/db.db: "..."` per folder, exit 0) and, in the old gufi_vt, a column list that names it (`Could not prepare '...' for getting column types`).
- An index from the 0.7.0 tag reads the same, with `Could not get isrolledup: no such column: canrollup` per folder on stderr, except where GUFI rolled a folder up: 0.8.0 (and the old pin) then list its entries more than once (969 rows for 324 distinct files).
- A tree of old and new directories (what a sync leaves) reads the same with either tool.

So I did not write a migration (a rename plus three recreated tables in every directory's database, in indexes that may hold vec0 tables, undoable, and fixing nothing the Studio reads) and did not add a rebuild on first start (hours on a large library for no change in any answer).

## What changes

- Every place GUFI is fetched is pinned to the 0.8.0 commit: `indexer/setup_gufi.sh` (`GUFI_REF` overrides), `deploy/app.def`, `deploy/make_bundle.sh` (a cached copy of another GUFI is fetched again), both ACTIVATE workflows (the clone is checked against the commit), `deploy/gufi-index.yaml` (both defaults), the macOS build, and the macOS package fallback (its URL returned 404, and the 0.8.0 package installs under `/Applications` with a link into the build machine, so `pkg_extract.py` gained `--drop-absolute-links`).
- Each library's format is read from its top summary table with the capability probe (`server/src/indexFormat.ts`), kept in `library-caps.json`, and for a library on another system taken from the `gufi_query` there at its connection test. Only the one case that reads wrongly is said out loud: an index from before the rename that has rolled-up folders is searched in part, named in the omissions line of Search and Query and in Settings, Libraries. A raw query naming `dev` on an older index gets one plain sentence.
- A new index is read by GUFI before it is swapped in (where `gufi_query` is there; the stand-in that tests use has none), and a stop between the two renames of a swap no longer leaves a library with no tree: the old one is put back at the next start.
- One Studio per index folder (`server/src/instanceLock.ts`). The second-launch test below found that a second Studio on the same data resumed the first one's interrupted build, cleared its staging folder, and left the first build `failed` with its tree moved aside. The second one now searches and queries, and answers index jobs with a 409 naming the first.
- A build that fails on a full disk or an unwritable folder says so in plain words and that the index in place is untouched.
- `indexer/setup_gufi.sh` on macOS (the from-source path for a clone): it already stopped at configure on origin/main, because CMake needs `flock` (run 41524269730 of `gufi-macos` with `check_setup_script`, old pin), and 0.8.0 asks for it too, so `flock` is installed and put on `PATH`. The next stop was llama.cpp (`errno` undeclared with the LLVM Homebrew installs now), so the C++ compiler is a wrapper that includes the headers the vendored code leaves out, as the app build does. With both, the script builds GUFI 0.8.0 on a macos-15 runner and indexes and queries; its last check, embedding with `gufi_sqlite3` and the model, segfaults (run 41535108165). See Open.
- `docs/HELP.md`, `docs/REFERENCE.md` (GUFI versions, one Studio per index folder), `docs/LIBRARIES.md`, `docs/GUFI-MACOS.md`, `README.md`. CHANGELOG untouched.
- Not done, noted in REFERENCE.md: `gufi_query --global-db` for the query embeddings of the search walk, and gufi_vt's `gufi_query=`.

## Test matrix

Linux host, GUFI 0.8.0 (`inst-new`), the pinned `1713537a` (`inst-old`) and the 0.7.0 tag (`inst-070`) built in user space; the Studio is this branch or origin/main. Each battery is 340 to 361 requests (19 searches by name, words, meaning, OCR, an external-table word; label filter; statistics; details; tree; six canned queries; eight builder forms; five SQL forms; the semantic map; labels; multi-library Query and search; history; the library listing), recorded before and after and compared section by section (rows as sets; ties among rows of equal size or time named). The fleet has the main folder at meaning-full and libraries at names, text, OCR, meaning-documents and meaning-full, one with a 0555 source, labels as xattrs and Studio-kept, `ext.db` tables, spaces, non-ASCII and a long path.

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Branch and 0.8.0 on a fleet built by the old GUFI and Studio | 311 identical, 24 ties, 0 different (main-branch code on 0.8.0 tools: 312, 23, 0) |
| Fleet built entirely by 0.8.0 against the old one | 296, 18, 0 |
| Fleet built by the 0.7.0 tag, read by the branch and 0.8.0 | 222, 13, 0 |
| History across the update | snapshots under both GUFIs: 324 files, nothing added, removed or modified |

| Connected indexes: rolled up by the old GUFI, by 0.8.0; written by 0.7.0, by the old GUFI, by 0.8.0 | identical in 48, 48, 46, 46, 45 sections. Rolled up by the 0.7.0 tag: both versions return the same wrong rows and only the branch says so (omissions line, Settings) |
| 0.8.0 Studio against a remote host on the old GUFI and on 0.8.0 (a local sshd; the GUFI is the library's bin directory), each reading an old-built and a 0.8.0-built index, with Query across local and remote through gufi_vt | remote old against remote 0.8.0: 80, 8, 0; gufi_vt answered and no library failed |
| Downgrade: old Studio and GUFI on a fleet built by 0.8.0; on a tree the new Studio synced | 318, 17, 0 and 334, 22, 0; nothing corrupted |
| Rebuild held in its text pass, server killed, restarted, held again, released | the index in place answered by name, words and meaning at every step; the resumed build equals a sync's result |

| Index folder on a 303 MB tmpfs holding 300 MB (user namespace, real ENOSPC) | `The disk the index is written on is full, so the new index was not finished. The index in place is untouched; free some space and rebuild.` Library keeps answering; rebuild succeeds once space is freed |

Suites: server 754 tests with the host's GUFI (748 pass, 6 skip), with none (610 pass, 144 skip, as CI runs them; CI's Linux and macOS test jobs pass) and with 0.8.0 (746 pass, 6 skip, 2 fail: `sshLibraries` and `restrictedRemote` look for GUFI at `/opt/gufi/bin`, and fail the same way on origin/main with a GUFI elsewhere); web 344 pass; `testdata` 21 pass. New tests: `indexFormat.test.mjs` (also run against the old GUFI and the 0.7.0-style schema it builds), `instanceLock.test.mjs`, a Settings row test.

## macOS

Run on this PR's head:

- `gufi-macos` (run 41515509805): GUFI 0.8.0 built for macOS 14 on macos-15 by `deploy/mac/build_gufi.sh`, then checked by `check_gufi.sh` on clean macos-14 and macos-26 runners (indexing, querying, gufi_vt, embedding with the model, search). It did not build as the script stood: GUFI 0.8.0 needs a static PCRE2 (`libpcre2-8.a`, so PCRE2 is now built shared and static), installs its dependencies' licenses from a folder its own script fills by download (now filled from the sources built here), installs `libvec0`, `liblembed0` and `libsqlite3` as links by absolute path into its build, and its `libdsi_querying` plugin has the run path `/lib` and `sqlite3-pcre` has none, which `macho_relink.py` cannot widen (now set with `install_name_tool` before the relink and re-signed). The 0.8.0 archive's manifest: macOS 14.0 target, SQLite 3.53.4, sqlite-vec 0.1.10-alpha.4, sqlite-lembed 0.0.1-alpha.8, PCRE2 10.49, libomp 23.1.4.
- `mac-app` (this PR's run, built with that archive through `GUFI_RUN`): the app builds with `GUFI 0.8.0 (021a717a6089) for macOS 14.0`, and `check_app.sh --run --launch --dmg` passes (351 checks, no failure), including the hardened-runtime copy: GUFI indexes a folder, `gufi_query` reads it, `gufi_sqlite3` embeds with the bundled model, the server runs from the app's run loop, and the launcher and LaunchAgent paths.
- `mac-upgrade-e2e` (new, `.github/scripts/mac-upgrade-e2e.sh`; on a pull request it waits for the same commit's mac-app run on a Linux runner and then runs on macos-15): installs the published v1.183 app (its bundled GUFI is the `macos-pkg-test` build), builds libraries of a small folder at names, text and meaning-documents, records 57 answers, quits the app, replaces it with this PR's app (GUFI 0.8.0), opens it on the same data, and checks that no index file was touched, that all 57 answers are unchanged, then rebuilds each library with 0.8.0 and checks the answers again. Passed: every `db.db` before the update had no `dev` column, after the rebuild each has one, 0 of 57 answers differ at either step. The existing #579 harnesses cannot do this (they update to the newest published release, not to an unpublished build), so this is a separate script. Its log prints the app's short version twice (both builds report 1.183); the server lines above it show the two commits.

## Before a release

Publish `gufi-macos-arm64` as the release `gufi-021a717-macos14` (push that tag), set `GUFI_RELEASE` in `mac-app.yml` to it and empty `GUFI_RUN` (a run's archive expires in 30 days). This PR points `GUFI_RUN` at the gufi-macos run that built 0.8.0 so its own mac-app run builds the app with it.

## v1.183 (2026-11-02)

### fix(mac): count a detach that already went through as done (#619)

The v1.182 PR build of the macOS app failed in make_dmg.sh after every app check had passed: `hdiutil detach` reported a failure, its retry found nothing there ("hdiutil: detach failed - No such file or directory"), and the script gave up. A detach that reports failure now counts as done when nothing is mounted at the mount point any more, checked against mount(8) by the mount point's real path (mktemp gives /var/..., mount prints /private/var/...). The rest of the retry and the forced detach are unchanged.

Checked: bash -n; the mac-app workflow runs on this PR and builds the disk image on a runner.

### fix(search): read external tables from the attached file by its alias (#622)

In gufi_query a directory's db.db is attached as `tree` and each file matched by `--external-copy` as `extdb` (a constant in GUFI). The Studio's external copy named `ext_bm25_by_file` and `ext_vectors_by_file` unqualified, and SQLite resolves an unqualified name to `tree` before `extdb`. A db.db holding tables of the same names (one proposed layout keeps group- and other-readable records there) was therefore read in place of the external file. The search walk (`gufi.ts`) and the remote semantic map (`remoteMap.ts`) now read `extdb.*`.

Test: searchOnePass.test.mjs adds a directory whose db.db and external file both carry `ext_bm25_by_file` with different text; search returns the external file's text. It fails without the change (it returned the db.db row). Server suite: 740 tests, 0 failed, 13 skipped.

### fix(setup): build GUFI on a clean Ubuntu and run setup_gufi.sh by relative path (#624)

Fixes the three `indexer/setup_gufi.sh` failures and the `docs/MACOS.md` inaccuracy found by running the README's own-machine steps on a clean `ubuntu:24.04`.

## Changes

- Package list: the apt line now installs `build-essential`, `git`, `curl`, `ca-certificates`, `python3` and `bsdextrautils` (provides `column`, which GUFI's cmake requires at configure time), and runs `apt-get update` first, since a clean image has no package lists. When the script runs as root (a container) it does not call `sudo`.
- `_FORTIFY_SOURCE`: GUFI's `src/gufi_query/spread_tree.c` calls `open(extdb_path, O_CREAT | O_WRONLY)` with no mode, which Ubuntu's default `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` rejects at compile time. After cloning GUFI, the script adds `S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR` to that call with `sed`. A source that already has a mode is left alone, so the step is a no-op once GUFI fixes the line. GUFI is not forked and no compiler flags change.
- Relative path: `PROJECT_ROOT` is computed at the top of the script, before any `cd`, so `indexer/setup_gufi.sh` now reaches the embedding model and ONNX fetch.
- `docs/MACOS.md`: `pnpm start` (`node server/dist/main.js`) and `server/src/config.ts` read `process.env` only and load no `.env` file. Only `deploy/run_endpoint.sh` sources `.env` (and the macOS app reads `studio.env`). The clone section now says so and shows `set -a; . ./.env; set +a` before `pnpm start`.
- README: the own-machine prerequisites now name git and say what `setup_gufi.sh` installs with apt (sudo unless root) or Homebrew.

## Upstream GUFI

The line is unchanged on upstream main (checked at 021a717, 29 Oct 2026) and at the commit pinned in `deploy/app.def` (468e572, 1 Oct 2026), so there is no upstream fix to bump to. The pin is not changed. The container build is on Debian, where the line compiles, and `setup_gufi.sh` is not part of it (`app.def` does its own GUFI step), so it is unaffected. The same sed would apply to the pinned commit if that image moved to Ubuntu.

## Verification

From a fresh clone of this branch in a clean `ubuntu:24.04` container (non-root user with sudo, 8 cores and 8 GB), with only Node 26.10.0 (checksummed tarball, plus `libatomic1`, which Node needs on the minimal image), git and curl installed beforehand, and no workarounds:

1. `npm install -g pnpm@11`, `pnpm install && pnpm build`.
2. `indexer/setup_gufi.sh` by relative path: apt step, GUFI build with AI dependencies, install to `/opt/gufi`, then the GGUF model and the ONNX backend fetched (about 9 minutes). The patched line was present in `~/gufi-src`.
3. `KB_ROOT=testdata/corpus indexer/reindex.sh`: 12 files indexed, 10 chunks embedded with `minilm-l6-mean-int8`.
4. `pnpm start`, `GET /api/version` returned 200, and `/api/search?q=invoice` returned the OCR text of the scanned invoice.

The container was removed afterwards. Not run here: the macOS path (the changes there are the relocated `PROJECT_ROOT` and the guarded sed, which uses `sed -i.orig` so it works with BSD and GNU sed) and the Debian container build.

## For #623

Once this merges, `docs/WINDOWS.md` can drop: the `CFLAGS=-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE` prefix on the `setup_gufi.sh` run and its explanation; the use of the full path in place of `indexer/setup_gufi.sh`; and, from the apt block, `build-essential`, `git`, `curl`, `ca-certificates`, `python3`, `bsdextrautils` and the other packages the script now installs (`cmake`, `pkg-config`, `attr`, `libattr1-dev`, `libsqlite3-dev`, `zlib1g-dev`, `libpcre2-dev`, `autoconf`, `automake`, `libtool`, `tesseract-ocr`, `poppler-utils`), leaving `git`, `curl` and `xz-utils` for the clone and the Node download. The paragraph explaining `bsdextrautils` can go with them, and the note that `pnpm start` does not read a `.env` stays accurate.

### docs: add Windows setup through WSL2 (#623)

Adds `docs/WINDOWS.md`, the steps for running the Studio on a Windows computer through WSL2 (or opening a Studio that runs on a Linux machine), and a Quick start line in the README plus a row in its documentation table.

## Not tested on Windows

The steps have not been run on a Windows machine. WSL behaviour described in the page (install command, `localhost` forwarding, `/mnt/c`, drvfs mounts, `.wslconfig`) comes from Microsoft's documentation, listed below, not from a run. Two points are not covered by those pages: that `mount -t drvfs ... -o ro` honours `ro` (the page states it without a caveat, so it needs a check on Windows), and what `setfattr` does on `/mnt/c` (the page tells the reader to check, and documents what the Studio does either way). The PowerShell one-liner that starts the server (`wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04 -e bash -c "exec ~/start-studio.sh"`) is also untested.

## What was verified, and how

The in-Ubuntu steps were run in a clean `ubuntu:24.04` Docker container (non-root user with sudo, limited to 8 cores and 8 GB to resemble a WSL2 default on a 16 GB computer), from a fresh clone of `origin/main` (2509396), by extracting the page's code blocks and running them unchanged:

1. The apt line, the Node 26.10.0 tarball with its checksum, `npm install -g pnpm@11`.
2. `git clone`, `pnpm install`, `pnpm build`, `CFLAGS=-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE ~/activate-studio/indexer/setup_gufi.sh` (542 s in total for steps 1 and 2, container peak memory 6.1 GB including page cache).
3. `KB_ROOT=~/activate-studio/testdata/corpus indexer/reindex.sh` (12 files indexed, 10 chunks embedded, the scanned PDF was read by tesseract).
4. The page's `start-studio.sh` and `studio.env`, then `curl http://127.0.0.1:4080/api/version` returned 200 with `v1.182`, and `/api/search?q=invoice` returned the OCR text of the scanned invoice.
5. The update commands (`git pull`, `pnpm install`, `pnpm build`) and the removal commands.

The sizing in the page comes from that run: clone 958 MB, GUFI source and build 1.1 GB, Node 252 MB, GUFI install 165 MB, server 0.17 GB RSS idle, and an index of 52 MB for a 7,500-file tree (about 7 KB per file for mostly non-text files).

## Problems found in the scripts, worked around in the page

A bare Ubuntu 24.04 fails `indexer/setup_gufi.sh` in three ways. The page works around each; the fixes belong in the script and README, and the page can then drop the workarounds.

- The script's own apt list lacks a compiler, git, curl, python3 and `bsdextrautils` (`column`, which GUFI's cmake requires at configure time). The page installs them first.
- GUFI's current `src/gufi_query/spread_tree.c` calls `open(path, O_CREAT | O_WRONLY)` without a mode, which Ubuntu's default `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` turns into a compile error. The commit pinned in `deploy/app.def` has the same line and builds there only because that image is Debian bookworm. The page sets `CFLAGS=-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE` for the first run.
- The script changes directory before computing `PROJECT_ROOT`, so `indexer/setup_gufi.sh` with a relative path (as the README's quick start shows) stops after the GUFI install and before fetching the embedding model. The page uses the full path.

Also seen while reading: `docs/MACOS.md` says to put settings in a `.env` at the repository root, but `pnpm start` does not read one (only `deploy/run_endpoint.sh` does), so the page uses a small script that sources `studio.env`.

## Microsoft documentation used for WSL facts

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install (Windows 10 2004, build 19041, or Windows 11; administrator PowerShell and restart; `wsl --install -d <Distro>`)
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/wsl-config (`.wslconfig` defaults: memory 50% of Windows memory, `localhostForwarding` true; `automount`, `/etc/fstab` processing; `networkingMode=mirrored`)
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/networking (`localhost` from Windows to Linux, the Windows host address from Linux via `ip route show`, mirrored mode, LAN access)
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/filesystems (keep Linux project files in the Linux file system, not `/mnt/c`)
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/file-permissions (drvfs metadata and the NTFS extended attributes it uses for permissions; nothing about `user.` xattrs)
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/basic-commands (`wsl --unregister` deletes all data, `wsl --shutdown`, `wsl --list --verbose`)
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/faq (error 0x800704ec from group policy, `/mnt/<drive>`, VM shuts down when idle)
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/blogs/wsl/file-system-improvements-to-the-windows-subsystem-for-linux (`sudo mount -t drvfs '\\server\share' /mnt/share`, no way to give a share credentials, network shares report 0777 and no symlinks)

## Labels on `/mnt/c`

The page describes the behaviour from the code: `server/src/tags.ts` writes `user.studio.tags` with `setfattr`, and when that fails the label goes to `tags-overlay.json` in the index folder, keyed by `st_dev.st_ino` with the birth time checked (`server/src/tagsOverlay.ts`). Other libraries always use the Studio's own label store (`docs/HELP.md`). Whether WSL2's `/mnt/c` accepts `user.` xattrs is not documented by Microsoft, so the page gives a one-line check instead of asserting it. How stable inode numbers are on drvfs across WSL restarts was not checked; if they change, overlay labels on `/mnt/c` files would be dropped as stale.
